adaptability.d: When this Pokémon uses a move of its own type, it may roll the damage twice and choose either total.

aftermath.d: This Pokémon deals damage to an attacker equal to half of the damage received when knocked out by a melee move.

air-lock.d: While this Pokémon is in battle, weather-related abilities have no effect on the Pokémon that have them.

analytic.d: After this Pokémon misses an attack, its next attack is done at advantage.

anger-point.d: After suffering a critical hit, this Pokémon doubles the damage dice for a single move it activates on the following turn.

anger-shell.d: When this Pokémon's HP drops below half its maximum HP, its AC drops by 2, but its STR and DEX scores each increase by 2, up to a maximum of 22. After a long rest, this Pokémon's AC, STR, and DEX return to their former values.

anticipation.d: When this Pokémon enters the battle, an opponent must reveal if it has a move that the Pokémon is vulnerable to. The move itself does not have to be revealed, only that there is such a move.

arena-trap.d: Grounded creatures within 50 feet of this Pokémon may not flee or switch out, except by item, Move, or ability.

armor-tail.d: While this Pokémon is out, hostile Pokémon within sight cannot use moves that require a bonus action to use.

aroma-veil.d: This Pokémon and its allies within 15 feet automatically passes any WIS save they are required to make.

as-one.d: Opponents in combat with this Pokémon cannot eat held berries. Upon causing an opponent to faint, this Pokémon may immediately move up to 20ft take another action. This ability cannot be swapped off this Pokémon.

aura-break.d: When this Pokémon is in battle, the boost of Fairy Aura and Dark Aura abilities is reversed, Any applicable move type activated within 100 feet deals half damage instead of double.

bad-dreams.d: If an opponent in battle with this Pokémon falls asleep, they take an amount of damage equal to this Pokémon's proficiency bonus at the end of each of their turns.

ball-fetch.d: This Pokémon has advantage catching or intercepting thrown/falling objects.

battery.d: Allies that activate electric-type moves within 20 feet of this Pokémon double their damage dice.

battle-armor.d: This Pokémon is immune to extra damage dealt by a Critical Hit.

beads-of-ruin.d: Creatures within 60ft of this Pokémon which do not have a "* of Ruin" ability have -4 Charisma score, to a minimum of 1. This effect does not stack, and the creature's Charisma score is restored upon leaving the area of effect.

beast-boost.d: Upon causing an opponent to faint, this Pokémon increases the ability scores of its saving throw proficiencies by 2 until the end of combat. This is stackable up to a maximum of +10 to any one ability score.

berserk.d: When this Pokémon falls below 25% of its maximum health, all of its attacks are rolled with disadvantage, but deal double their damage. If a move activated requires a saving throw, the target(s) have advantage on the roll.

big-pecks.d: This Pokémon's AC cannot be reduced by an opponent's moves.

blaze.d: This Pokémon doubles its STAB bonus when it has 25% or less of its maximum health.

bulletproof.d: This Pokémon is immune to damage from moves with Bullet, Ball, or Bomb in their name.

cheek-pouch.d: When this Pokémon eats any type of berry, it heals for an additional 10% of its maximum HP (rounded up to the nearest whole number).

chilling-neigh.d: Upon causing an opponent to faint, this Pokémon may immediately move up to 20ft take another action.

chlorophyll.d: This Pokémon’s speed is doubled in harsh sunlight.

clear-body.d: Other Pokémon's moves or abilities cannot lower this Pokémon stats.

cloud-nine.d: While this Pokémon is in battle, weather-related abilities have no effect on the Pokémon that have them.

color-change.d: When hit by a damaging attack, this Pokémon's type changes to the type that hit it. It takes on the new type's resistances, vulnerabilities, and immunities.

comatose.d: This Pokémon is in a continuous state of drowsiness. It is immune to the sleep condition, but is considered affected by sleep for all moves that require a Pokémon to be asleep to use or activate additional effects (Snore, Sleep Talk, Wake-Up Slap, Dream Eater, etc.)

commander.d: Once per long rest, this Pokémon may use its action to leap into the mouth of a nearby Dondozo. While in the mouth, this Pokémon may not take actions that target creatures or objects outside of Dondozo's body; additionally, it cannot itself be targeted. While in the mouth, the Dondozo gains proficiency to WIS saves. This Pokémon may use an action to leave Dondozo's mouth, or it is ejected from the mouth at an adjacent space if Dondozo faints.

competitive.d: This Pokémon adds its proficiency bonus to damage rolls while poisoned, burned, confused, or paralyzed.

compound-eyes.d: This Pokémon gets an additional +1 to attack rolls.

contrary.d: Moves that affect this Pokémon's stats have the opposite effect. (For example, Defense Curl would lower AC by 4. Growl would increase its attack by +1)

corrosion.d: This Pokémon's moves ignore the poison immunity of creatures granted by their Pokémon type, and can inflict the poisoned status on poison and steel type creatures. If the target’s secondary type gives it vulnerability or resistance to the damage, it follows the secondary type for that effect.

costar.d: When this Pokémon is within 5ft of an ally, it has advantage on its attack rolls.

cotton-down.d: When this Pokémon is damaged, cotton spews everywhere. The area within 10ft of this Pokémon becomes difficult terrain for everything except Grass monotypes until the beginning of its next turn.

cud-chew.d: After consuming a berry, on the following turn, this Pokémon may consume the berry a second time, thereafter consuming it permanently.

curious-medicine.d: As a bonus action, this Pokémon can reset changes to the ability scores, AC, and attack modifier of either itself or an ally within 30 ft. This Pokémon may do this a number of times equal to its INT modifier (minimum of once), and it resets on a long rest.

cursed-body.d: When hit by a melee attack, this Pokémon may roll 1d4. On a result of 4, the opponent who made the attack cannot use the same move on its next turn.

cute-charm.d: Once per short rest, you can impose disadvantage on an enemy attack roll of your choice.

damp.d: This Pokémon is unaffected by Self Destruct and Explosion moves.

dancer.d: If any creature within sight of this Pokémon activates a move with Dance in its name, this Pokémon may immediately use one of its moves as a reaction.

dark-aura.d: When this Pokémon is in battle, all dark-type moves by allies or opponents within 100 feet deal double their damage.

dauntless-shield.d: Melee attacks made against this Pokémon have disadvantage.

dazzling.d: Creatures within line of sight of this Pokémon cannot use bonus actions to activate Moves. Moves that would normally have a Move Time of "1 bonus action" instead have a Move Time of "1 action".

defeatist.d: When this Pokémon drops below 25% of its maximum HP, all of its attacks are rolled with disadvantage.

defiant.d: While this Pokémon is suffering from a negative status effect or stat change imposed by an opponent, it gains +2 to all attack rolls.

desolate-land.d: For as long as this Pokémon is engaged in combat, the weather is Extremely Harsh Sunlight and cannot be changed. Extremely Harsh Sunlight is the same as Harsh Sunlight, with the additional effect that Water-type damage is nullified. If Primordial Sea is also active, then the weather is simultaneously Extremely Harsh Sunlight and Heavy Rain.

disguise.d: This Pokémon has a disguise which gives it a temporary hp boost equal to twice its level. When the temporary hit points fall to zero, the disguise breaks and requires a short rest to repair.

download.d: Once per short rest, this Pokémon can choose a different damage type for one of their normal attacks.

dragons-maw.d: When this Pokémon uses a dragon-type move, it may roll the damage twice and choose either total.

drifter.d: In windy conditions (DM discretion), this Pokémon's flying (hover) speed is doubled until windy conditions cease.

drizzle.d: When this Pokémon enters an outside battle, the weather immediately changes to light rain for 5 rounds. In the case of another Pokémon with a similar weather ability, the tie goes to the Pokémon with the highest DEX score.

drought.d: When this Pokémon enters an outside battle, the weather immediately changes to bright sunlight for 5 rounds. In the case of another Pokémon with a similar weather ability, the tie goes to the Pokémon with the highest DEX score.

dry-skin.d: At the end of each of this Pokémon's turns, it takes an amount of damage equal to its proficiency modifier in harsh sunlight, or heals for the same amount during rain.

early-bird.d: This Pokémon has advantage on the D20 roll to wake from the asleep condition.

earth-eater.d: This Pokémon takes no damage from ground-type attacks. Instead, half of any ground damage done is absorbed, restoring the Pokémon's HP.

effect-spore.d: When hit by a melee attack, roll a d4. On a 4, deal an amount of grass damage equal to your proficiency modifier to your attacker.

electric-surge.d: If the move is known, this Pokémon may use the Electric Terrain move as a bonus action.

electromorphosis.d: When this Pokémon takes damage, it may double the MOVE damage modifier of its next electric-type move.

embody-aspect-cornerstone.d: This Pokémon automatically gains this ability when Terastallized. This Pokémon's CON score becomes 23, unless it is already higher.

embody-aspect-heartflame.d: This Pokémon automatically gains this ability when Terastallized. This Pokémon's STR score becomes 23, unless it is already higher.

embody-aspect-teal.d: This Pokémon automatically gains this ability when Terastallized. This Pokémon's DEX score becomes 23, unless it is already higher.

embody-aspect-wellspring.d: This Pokémon automatically gains this ability when Terastallized. This Pokémon's CHA score becomes 23, unless it is already higher.

emergency-exit.d: At any time this Pokémon is damaged when it is at or below 50% of its maximum HP, its trainer may switch it out as a free action.

fairy-aura.d: When this Pokémon is in battle, all fairy-type moves within 100 feet of you deal double their damage.

filter.d: When hit by a move type this Pokémon is vulnerable to, it may roll a d4. In a result of 4, it does not take the additional damage.

flame-body.d: The flames from this Pokémon's body shine dim light in a 15 ft radius. In addition, when hit by a melee attack, roll a d10. On a 10, the attacker is burned.

flare-boost.d: This Pokémon adds proficiency to its damage rolls while burned.

flash-fire.d: This Pokémon takes no damage from fire or fire-type attacks. Instead, immediately after taking a hit from a fire-type move, or in open flames, double the STAB bonus on the next fire-type move.

flower-gift.d: During harsh sunlight, ally Pokémon within 30 feet of this Pokémon add their proficiency bonus to damage rolls.

flower-veil.d: This Pokémon's grass-type allies within 15 feet (including itself if it is grass-type) are immune to new status effects.

fluffy.d: This Pokemon is vulnerable to fire-type moves, but takes half damage from any melee attack (that isn't fire-type).

forecast.d: This Pokémon changes form with the weather. In rain it becomes water-type, in harsh sunlight it becomes fire-type, in cold and snowy conditions it becomes ice-type. In all other conditions it is normal-type. Its STAB, resistance, immunities, and vulnerabilities change to match the form it takes.

forewarn.d: When this Pokémon enters battle, it selects a target to reveal the move it knows with the most damage output. In the case of a tie, the target can choose which move it reveals.

friend-guard.d: Once per long rest, when an ally within 15 feet of this Pokémon is hit by an attack, it may choose to halve the damage dealt.

frisk.d: Upon entering a battle, a single opponent’s held item is revealed, if it has one.

full-metal-body.d: Other Pokémon's moves or abilities cannot lower this Pokémon stats.

fur-coat.d: Once per long rest, this Pokémon may halve the damage dealt to it from any one attack.

gale-wings.d: This Pokémon adds an additional +1 to hit when using flying-type attacks.

galvanize.d: All of this Pokémon's normal-type moves are electric-type.

gluttony.d: This Pokémon must eat its held berry when it falls below ½ of its maximum HP.

good-as-gold.d: This Pokémon is immune to status effects.

gooey.d: When this Pokémon is hit with a melee attack, roll 1d4. On a result of 3 or 4, the attacker's speed is reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn.

gorilla-tactics.d: When this Pokémon enters the battlefield, choose one of its moves. Double the MOVE damage modifier for the selected move; the MOVE damage modifier for this Pokémon's other moves becomes 0. The effect resets when this Pokémon leaves the battlefield.

grass-pelt.d: This Pokémon gains +1 to AC while in grassy terrain.

grassy-surge.d: If the move is known, this Pokémon may use the Grassy Terrain move as a bonus action.

grim-neigh.d: Upon causing an opponent to faint, this Pokémon may immediately move up to 20ft take another action.

guard-dog.d: This Pokémon cannot be forcibly switched out by other moves. Intimidation rolls made against this Pokémon have disadvantage. This Pokémon is unaffected by the Intimidate ability.

gulp-missile.d: May Grapple as a bonus action after completing either Surf or Dive. As a bonus action, may launch a creature grappled by you up to 15ft, dealing fall damage equivalent to the distance launched.

guts.d: When this Pokémon is burned or poisoned, they are not affected by the disadvantage or reduced damage effects. They still take damage at the end of each of their turns. Additionally, while it is burned, poisoned, paralyzed, frozen, or asleep, it gains +2 to all attack and damage rolls it makes for moves with a melee attack roll.

hadron-engine.d: As a bonus action, this Pokémon may change the terrain to electric terrain for 5 rounds; this bonus action may be used twice per short rest. In electric terrain, this Pokémon has advantage on attack rolls using DEX or WIS as the move power.

harvest.d: At the end of this Pokémon's turn, if it used a berry, roll 1d4. On a result of 3 or 4, it regains that berry as a held item.

healer.d: As an action, this Pokemon may touch a creature to heal poison, burn, or paralysis. When it uses this ability, roll a d4. On the a result of 1 or 2, the status effect is moved to itself.

heatproof.d: This Pokemon takes half the damage it otherwise would from Fire damage, and is immune to the burning condition.

heavy-metal.d: This Pokémon is especially heavy. Once per long rest, after being targeted by an attack, it may increase its AC by 2 if it would cause an attack to miss.

honey-gather.d: At the end of each battle, this Pokémon may roll a d20 + its proficiency bonus. On a result of 20 or higher, its trainer adds a Honey to their inventory.

hospitality.d: At the start of its turn, all allies within 20ft of this Pokémon gain 1d4 temporary HP. This replaces existing temporary HP.

huge-power.d: Once per short rest, this Pokémon may double the damage dice for a single damage roll. The player must announce that they are using this ability before the attack roll.

hunger-switch.d: At the start of its turn, this Pokemon switches to Hangry Mode if it was in Full Belly Mode, or switches to Full Belly Mode if it was in Hangry Mode.

hustle.d: When you score a critical hit, you may immediately gain an additional action on your turn. If this action is used to make an attack, you have disadvantage on the roll. You may only ever have one additional action per round.

hydration.d: This Pokémon is unaffected by negative status ailments in water or during rainy conditions.

hyper-cutter.d: This Pokémon’s attack or damage bonuses cannot be decreased by an opponent’s moves.

ice-body.d: While it is snowing or hailing, this Pokémon heals for an amount of HP equal to its proficiency modifier at the end of each of its turns. This Pokémon takes no damage from hail.

ice-face.d: This Pokémon has two forms: Ice Form and No-Ice Form. When in Ice Form, the first time this pokémon takes damage, it takes half that damage but transforms into No-Ice Form. When in No-Ice Form, this pokemon's AC is decreased by 3 and each of its movement speeds are increased by 5 ft. This Pokémon reverts back to Ice Form after a short rest, or on the start of its turn when in the hail.

ice-scales.d: This Pokémon has resistance to damange dealt by moves whose power is one of INT, WIS, or CHA.

illuminate.d: This Pokémon knows the Light cantrip and can cast it at will.

illusion.d: This Pokémon can take the visual form of any Pokémon it can see. It can do this a number of times per long rest equal to its level. This illusion lasts for one hour or until the Pokémon is hit by a damaging move.

immunity.d: This Pokémon is immune to becoming poisoned.

imposter.d: This Pokémon can use Transform as a bonus action.

infiltrator.d: This Pokémon bypasses Light Screen, Reflect, Substitute, Mist, Safeguard, and Aurora Veil.

innards-out.d: When this Pokémon is knocked out by a damaging move, the attacker takes an amount of typeless damage equal to the amount of HP lost.

inner-focus.d: This Pokémon is immune to flinching.

insomnia.d: This Pokémon is immune to sleep.

intimidate.d: Once per short rest, you can impose disadvantage on an enemy attack roll of your choice.

intrepid-sword.d: This Pokémon makes melee attacks with advantage.

iron-barbs.d: When this Pokémon is hit by a melee attack, it may roll a d4. On a 4, deal an amount of steel damage equal to its proficiency modifier to its attacker.

iron-fist.d: When attacking with a punch-based move (Mega Punch, Dynamic Punch, Ice/Fire/Thunder Punch, etc.), this Pokémon may roll the damage twice and choose either total.

justified.d: When this Pokémon is hit by a dark-type move, it gets advantage on its next attack.

keen-eye.d: This Pokémon ignores disadvantage when it relates to sight.

klutz.d: This Pokémon cannot hold an item.

leaf-guard.d: This Pokémon does not suffer from any negative status ailments in harsh sunlight.

levitate.d: This Pokémon is immune to ground moves.

libero.d: While executing a move, this Pokémon's type becomes the same as that of the move and may add its STAB bonus to it.

light-metal.d: This Pokémon is especially light for its species. Once per long rest, it may impose disadvantage on an attack roll against it.

lightning-rod.d: If this Pokemon or an ally within 30 feet is targeted with a direct electric-type, damage-dealing move, the Pokemon may use a reaction to redirect the target to itself and take half damage from it if it hits.

limber.d: This Pokémon is immune to being paralyzed.

lingering-aroma.d: When this Pokémon is hit by a melee attack or hits with a melee attack, one random ability of its attacker changes to Lingering Aroma until the end of the encounter or until switched out.

liquid-ooze.d: If an enemy uses a leeching or absorb move against this Pokémon, the Pokémon must make a DC 12 CON save or become poisoned.

liquid-voice.d: Any sound-based move activated by this Pokémon is water-type.

long-reach.d: This Pokémon has an additional 5 feet of reach with all melee attacks and Attacks of Opportunity.

magic-bounce.d: Once per long rest, when succumbing to a negative status effect, this Pokémon can instead reflect the effect back on the attacker.

magic-guard.d: If this Pokémon is subjected to a move that forces it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage on a success.

magician.d: If not already holding an item, this Pokémon steals the held item of any Pokémon it hits with a melee attack.

magma-armor.d: This Pokémon is immune to freezing.

magnet-pull.d: Steel opponents in battle with this Pokémon may not switch out or flee.

marvel-scale.d: This Pokémon's AC increase by 2 when suffering from a negative status condition.

mega-launcher.d: Aura and Pulse moves made by this Pokémon deal additional damage/healing equal to this Pokémon's proficiency bonus.

merciless.d: This Pokémon doubles their damage dice when dealing damage to an opponent that is poisoned.

mimicry.d: This Pokémon's type changes depending on the terrain. If a Terrain move is active, this Pokémon's type becomes the Terrain move's type. This Pokémon's type reverts once the Terrain move deactivates.

minds-eye.d: This Pokémon ignores immunity to its Normal- and Fighting-type moves. It also ignores disadvantage on attacks it makes against targets it can see.

minus.d: This Pokémon boosts its attack and damage rolls by 2 if an ally also has a Plus or Minus ability

mirror-armor.d: When affected by an effect that lowers this Pokémon's attack roll, AC, movement, or ability scores, the same effect is applied to the source (if applicable).

misty-surge.d: If the move is known, this Pokémon may use the Misty Terrain move as a bonus action.

mold-breaker.d: This Pokémon's moves ignore any abilities that would lessen their effect or ability to hit an opponent (Due to things like Water Absorb, Snow Cloak, Thick Fat, Sturdy, etc.)

moody.d: At the end of each long rest, this Pokémon rerolls on the nature table, replacing its nature with the result until the next long rest.

motor-drive.d: When hit by an electric-type move, if not immune, this Pokémon's speed increases by 10 feet until the end of combat (up to a max of 50 additional feet).

moxie.d: Upon causing an opponent to faint, this Pokémon may immediately take another action.

multiscale.d: If this Pokémon is at full health, the first damage dealt to it is halved.

multitype.d: This Pokémon's type and form change to match the type of Elemental Plate this Pokémon holds. The Plate cannot be affected by any item-removing ability or move.

mummy.d: When this Pokémon is hit by a melee attack, one random ability of its attacker changes to Mummy for the remainder of the encounter.

mycelium-might.d: Once per short rest, when causing a creature to make a save that inflicts a status condition on failure, this Pokémon may invoke Mycelium Might to cause that creature to roll the save with disadvantage.

natural-cure.d: This Pokémon is cured of negative status ailments upon returning to its Pokeball.

neuroforce.d: When this Pokémon damages a creature with a super effective move, it may roll the damage dice twice and use the higher result.

neutralizing-gas.d: The abilities of Pokémon within 30ft of this Pokémon are nullified and cannot trigger. This nullification does not apply to the Neutralizing Gas ability or any form changes.

no-guard.d: Any attack made by or against this Pokémon has advantage.

normalize.d: Every move this Pokémon activates is Normal type.

oblivious.d: This Pokémon is immune to moves that attempt to charm or taunt it.

opportunist.d: When the AC, STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS, or CHA of an enemy this Pokémon can see increases, then this Pokémon's corresponding attribute increases by the same amount. This effect lasts for the duration of battle, or for 1 minute.

orichalcum-pulse.d: As a bonus action, this Pokémon may change the weather to harsh sunlight for 5 rounds; this bonus action may be used twice per short rest. In harsh sunlight, this Pokémon has advantage on attack rolls using STR or CON as the move power.

overcoat.d: This Pokémon does not take damage from weather-related moves and phenomena like Hail, Weather Ball, etc.

overgrow.d: This Pokémon doubles its STAB bonus when it has 25% or less of its maximum health.

own-tempo.d: This Pokémon is immune to becoming confused.

paper-thin.d: This Pokémon always has a maximum HP of 1. (Shedinja only. Cannot be passed or swapped)

pastel-veil.d: This Pokémon and its allies cannot be poisoned for as long as it is in combat.

perish-body.d: When hit by a melee attack, this Pokémon and its attacker will faint in 3 rounds, at the start of their respective turn, unless fleeing or switched out by their trainer before the end of the three rounds.

pickpocket.d: When hit by a melee attack, this Pokémon may use a reaction to attempt to steal the creature's held item with a Sleight of Hand check contested by the target's Passive Perception. After the first attempt, all other attempts against the same opponent are rolled at disadvantage.

pickup.d: If an opponent uses a consumable held item in battle, this Pokémon gains a copy of it if it is not currently holding an item.

pixilate.d: All of this Pokémon's normal-type moves become fairy-type.

plus.d: This Pokémon boosts its attack and damage rolls by 2 if an ally also has a Plus or Minus ability

poison-heal.d: This Pokémon does not suffer the disadvantage effects of the poisoned status condition. Additionally, when this pokemon would take poison-type damage or damage from the poisoned condition, it instead recovers HP equal to half the damage it would have taken.

poison-point.d: When this Pokémon is hit with a melee attack, roll a 1d4. On a result of 4, the attacker takes an amount of poison damage equal to this Pokémon’s proficiency modifier.

poison-puppeteer.d: When this Pokémon inflicts the Poisoned or Badly Poisoned condition, it also inflicts the Charmed condition. Creatures charmed this way may attempt to break from the charm at the end of each of their turns with a CHA save against this Pokémon's CHA DC.

poison-touch.d: On melee attacks made by this Pokémon, roll a d10 on a hit. On a result of a 10, the target is poisoned.

power-construct-10.d: When Zygarde 10% is reduced to less than half of its maximum HP, it changes to Zygarde 50% Forme and recovers all hit points.

power-construct-50.d: When Zygarde 50% is reduced to less than half of its maximum HP, it changes to Complete Forme and recovers all hit points.

power-construct-100.d: When Zygarde is reduced to less than half of its maximum HP, it changes to Complete Forme and stays in that form, regardless of HP changes.

power-of-alchemy.d: When switched in after an ally faints, this Pokémon copies the non-hidden ability of the fainted ally until switched out.

power-spot.d: Allies within 15 ft of this Pokemon may add 1d6 to damage they deal from moves. This die may only be used once per move per turn. At level 10, the bonus damage becomes 1d8 instead.

prankster.d: Once per short rest, when a round begins during combat, this Pokémon can choose to take its turn this round before any other creatures; when it does, it cannot use any damaging Moves against other creatures during that turn.

pressure.d: Any move targeting this Pokémon directly (non-area of effect moves) reduces its PP by two when activated.

primordial-sea.d: For as long as this Pokémon is engaged in combat, the weather is Heavy Rain and cannot be changed. Heavy Rain is the same as Rain, with the additional effect that Fire-type damage is nullified. If Desolate Land is also active, then the weather is simultaneously Extremely Harsh Sunlight and Heavy Rain.

prism-armor.d: When this Pokémon is subject to damage in its vulnerabilities list, roll the damage dice twice and use the lower result for the damage calculation.

propeller-tail.d: This Pokémon's ignores the effects of moves that alters the targets of its own moves (such as Follow Me).

protean.d: This Pokémon's type changes to the type of move it uses, just before the move is used. It takes on the new type's resistances, vulnerabilities, and immunities.

protosynthesis.d: This Pokémon may have a STR and CON scores up to 22. In harsh sunlight, this Pokémon has advantage on STR and CON saves.

psychic-surge.d: If the move is known, this Pokémon may use the Psychic Terrain move as a bonus action.

punk-rock.d: When this Pokémon uses a sound-based move, it adds its STAB bonus to the damage. This Pokémon has resistance to sound-based moves.

pure-power.d: Once per short rest, this Pokémon may double the damage dice for a single damage roll. The player must announce that they are using this ability before the attack roll.

purifying-salt.d: This Pokémon has resistance to Ghost-type damage, and it cannot be afflicted with non-volatile status conditions.

quark-drive.d: This Pokémon may have a DEX and WIS scores up to 22. On electric terrain, this Pokémon has advantage on DEX and WIS saves.

queenly-majesty.d: Creatures within line of sight of this Pokémon cannot use bonus actions to activate Moves. Moves that would normally have a Move Time of "1 bonus action" instead have a Move Time of "1 action".

quick-draw.d: This Pokémon has advantage on initiative rolls.

quick-feet.d: When suffering from a negative status condition, this Pokémon’s speed increases by 15 ft.

rain-dish.d: In rainy conditions, this Pokémon heals for an amount of HP equal to its proficiency bonus at the end of each of its turns.

rattled.d: When this Pokémon is hit by a damaging Dark, Bug, or Ghost move, it makes its next attack at advantage.

receiver.d: When switched in after an ally faints, this Pokémon copies the non-hidden ability of the fainted ally until switched out.

reckless.d: When attacking with moves with recoil damage, this Pokémon doubles its STAB bonus.

refrigerate.d: All of this Pokémon's normal-type moves become ice-type.

regenerator.d: Once per long rest, this Pokémon regains hit points equal to its level when it returns to its Pokéball.

ripen.d: Doubles the effects of berries consumed.

rivalry.d: This Pokémon adds its proficiency bonus to damage when attacking a Pokémon of the same type.

rks-system.d: This Pokémon's type is determined by the memory disc it holds. If not holding a memory disc, this Pokémon's type is normal.

rock-head.d: This Pokémon takes no recoil damage.

rocky-payload.d: When this Pokémon uses a rock-type move, it may roll the damage twice and choose either total.

rough-skin.d: When this Pokémon is hit by a melee attack, it may roll a d4. On a 4, deal an amount of typeless damage equal to its proficiency modifier to its attacker.

run-away.d: This Pokémon cannot be the target of an attack of opportunity.

sand-force.d: This Pokémon is immune to Sandstorm damage. During a Sandstorm, this Pokémon can double its STAB when it hits an opponent.

sand-rush.d: This Pokémon is immune to Sandstorm damage, and its speed is doubled in desert terrain, or during a Sandstorm.

sand-spit.d: When this Pokémon takes damage, it may use its reaction to cause a Sandstorm centered on self with a radius of 30ft. The Sandstorm lasts for five rounds. The Pokémon may do this a number of times equal to its proficiency bonus, and it resets after a long rest.

sand-stream.d: When this Pokémon enters an outside battle, the weather immediately changes to a Sandstorm for 5 rounds. In the case of another Pokémon with a similar weather ability, the tie goes to the Pokémon with the highest DEX score.

sand-veil.d: This Pokémon is immune to Sandstorm damage. In addition, its AC increases by 2 in desert terrain, or during a Sandstorm.

sap-sipper.d: This Pokémon takes no damage from grass-type attacks. If hit by a grass type move, it takes no damage and instead absorbs the energy, granting advantage on its next attack.

schooling.d: Beginning at level 5, this Pokémon may change to School Form as a free action when it begins its turn above 25% of its maximum health. In School Form, the Pokémon adds 5 to its AC and Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution ability scores (Additional CON does not alter this Pokemon's HP in this form). The Pokémon reverts back to Solo Form when it falls below 25% of maximum health, and must complete a short rest before activating this ability again.

scrappy.d: This Pokémon's Normal and Fighting type moves ignore immunities granted by a Pokémon's type. If a target’s secondary type gives it vulnerability or resistance to the attack, it follows the secondary type for that effect.

screen-cleaner.d: Light Screen, Reflect, and Aurora Veil have no effect within 40ft of this Pokémon.

seed-sower.d: When hit by a damaging attack, this Pokémon may use its reaction to use the Grassy Terrain move. The Pokémon does not need to know this move, and it costs no PP to use. This may be used up to three times per long rest.

serene-grace.d: The Move DC to pass a saving throw against one of this Pokémon's moves is increased by 2.

shadow-shield.d: If this Pokémon is at full health, the first damage dealt to it is halved.

shadow-tag.d: Creatures within 50 feet of this Pokémon may not flee or switch out, except by item, Move, or ability.

sharpness.d: Moves with 'Cut', 'Blade', 'Slash', 'Edge', 'Cleave', 'Razor', 'Sword', or 'Axe' in their name have their MOVE damage modifier doubled.

shed-skin.d: If this Pokémon is affected by a negative status ailment, they can roll a d4 at the end of each of their turns. On a result of 4, they are cured.

sheer-force.d: When activating a move that has a chance to impose a stat change or inflict a status, this creature instead doubles its MOVE modifier (not STAB) for the damage with no chance of the additional effect.

shell-armor.d: This Pokémon is immune to extra damage dealt by a Critical Hit.

shield-dust.d: Once per long rest, this Pokémon can ignore a negative status condition that results from an enemy move.

shields-down.d: This Pokémon is immune to Non-Volatile status effects while in Meteor Form. When this Pokémon falls below 50% of its maximum hp, its outer shell breaks and it changes to Core Form. In Core Form, it adds 6 points to its DEX, but reduces its AC by 4. The Pokémon must complete a short rest to restore itself to Meteor Form.

simple.d: Once per short rest, you may double this Pokémon's Move modifier for a single attack or damage roll.

skill-link.d: Combo moves that have the ability to hit more than once, after the same attack roll, are guaranteed to hit at least twice. (Fury Swipes, Double Slap, Water Shuriken, etc.)

slow-start.d: During the first two rounds of each combat, this Pokémon's speed is halved and its attacks are made at disadvantage.

slush-rush.d: This Pokémon is immune to Hail damage, and its speed is doubled in arctic conditions, or during a hailstorm.

sniper.d: On a critical hit made by this Pokémon, triple the dice roll instead of doubling it.

snow-cloak.d: This Pokémon is immune to Hail damage. It's AC is increased by 2 in arctic conditions, or when it is snowing or hailing.

snow-warning.d: When this Pokémon enters an outside battle, the weather immediately changes to hail for 5 rounds. In the case of another Pokémon with a similar weather ability, the tie goes to the Pokémon with the highest DEX score.

solar-power.d: Damage rolls for this Pokémon get an additional +2 during harsh sunlight.

solid-rock.d: This Pokémon does not take any additional damage from a critical hit.

soul-heart.d: Upon seeing an ally faint, this Pokémon increases the ability scores of its saving throw proficiencies by 2 until the end of combat. This is stackable up to a maximum of +10 to any one ability score.

soundproof.d: This Pokémon is immune to sound-based moves.

speed-boost.d: This Pokémon's speed is increased by 10 feet while in an environment related to its type (DM Discretion).

stakeout.d: When an opponent is switched out in battle, until the end of this Pokémon's next turn following the switch, it doubles the damage it deals to the replacement.

stall.d: This Pokémon is always last in initiative order.

stalwart.d: This Pokémon may always choose its targets, ignoring the effects of moves that redirect targetting.

stamina.d: When this Pokémon is damaged by a move, increase its AC by 2 until the start of its next turn. This ability does not stack and will remain in effect if the Pokémon is successfully attacked multiple turns in a row.

stance-change.d: Aegislash has two forms. When Aegislash uses King's Shield, even if the reaction is unsucessful, it changes to Shield Forme, swapping its AC and DEX stats. When it uses a damaging move, Aegislash immediately returns to Blade Forme, returning its stats to normal.

static.d: When this Pokémon is hit by a melee attack, roll a d4. On a result of 4, the attacker takes an amount of electric damage equal to this Pokemon's proficiency bonus.

steadfast.d: Once per long rest, when this Pokémon fails a saving throw against a negative condition, it can choose to pass instead.

steam-engine.d: When damaged by a Fire- or Water-type move, this Pokémon's walking speed becomes double its base value until the end of its next turn.

steelworker.d: This Pokémon adds its proficiency bonus to damage dealt by steel-type moves.

steely-spirit.d: This Pokémon and allies of this Pokémon within 30ft of it boost the damage roll of their Steel-type moves by this Pokémon's CHA modifier. This effect may stack up to two times.

stench.d: When this Pokémon is hit by a melee attack, roll a d10. On a 10, the attacker flinches.

sticky-hold.d: Held items cannot be stolen or knocked away from this Pokémon.

storm-drain.d: If this Pokemon or an ally within 30 feet is targeted with a direct water-type, damage-dealing move, the Pokemon may use a reaction to redirect the target to itself and take half damage from it if it hits.

strong-jaw.d: For biting moves activated by this Pokémon (Bite, Thunder Fang, Crunch, etc.), they may roll the damage twice and choose either total.

sturdy.d: When taking damage equal to half or more of your current HP, roll a d4. On a result of 3 or 4, halve the damage dealt.

suction-cups.d: This Pokémon cannot be forced out of battle by an opponent’s moves.

super-luck.d: This Pokémon increases its critical hit range by 1 (20 to 19+, etc.)

supersweet-syrup.d: Attack rolls made against creatures within 30ft of this Pokémon gain 1d4 on the roll. Creatures with no sense of smell are not affected by this ability.

supreme-overlord.d: This Pokémon adds +1 to its attack rolls for each currently downed ally, up to a maximum of +5.

surge-surfer.d: When this Pokémon begins its turn in the area of effect from Electric Terrain, its speed is doubled until the start of its next turn.

swarm.d: This Pokémon doubles its STAB bonus when it has 25% or less of its maximum health.

sweet-veil.d: This Pokémon and its allies within 15 feet are immune to the sleep condition.

swift-swim.d: This Pokémon's speed is doubled in rainy conditions.

sword-of-ruin.d: Creatures within 60ft of this Pokémon which do not have a "* of Ruin" ability have -4 Constitution score, to a minimum of 1. This effect does not stack, and the creature's Constitution score is restored upon leaving the area of effect.

symbiosis.d: This Pokémon may swap held items with an ally as a free action, as long as they are within 15 feet of each other.

synchronize.d: If this Pokémon becomes burned, paralyzed, or poisoned, its attacker receives the negative status condition as well (if not immune).

tablets-of-ruin.d: Creatures within 60ft of this Pokémon which do not have a "* of Ruin" ability have -4 Strength score, to a minimum of 1. This effect does not stack, and the creature's Strength score is restored upon leaving the area of effect.

tangled-feet.d: Attacks against this Pokémon have disadvantage when it is confused.

tangling-hair.d: Opponents within melee range of this Pokémon cannot take the Disengage action to move away.

technician.d: For damaging moves activated by this Pokémon with 15 max PP or more, they may roll the damage twice and choose either total.

telepathy.d: This Pokémon cannot be damaged by its allies' attacks.

tera-shell.d: While Terapagos is at full HP, it is resistant to all damage types.

tera-shift.d: Terapagos can shift into its Terastal form a number of times per day equal to its CON modifier as a free action. It reverts to its normal form after 10 minutes or at will.

teraform-zero.d: While Terapagos is in its Stellar Form, all terrain and weather effects within 1000ft end, and the terrain and weather cannot be changed.

teravolt.d: This Pokémon’s moves completely ignore any ability that would hinder or prevent their effect on the target or the user's ability to hit the target.

thermal-exchange.d: This Pokémon cannot be burned. When this Pokémon takes fire-type damage, it makes its next attack with advantage.

thick-fat.d: This Pokemon takes half the damage it otherwise would from Ice and Fire damage.

torrent.d: This Pokémon doubles its STAB bonus when it has 25% or less of its maximum health.

tough-claws.d: A successful melee attack by this Pokémon automatically gets STAB, regardless of its type. If it would normally get STAB, double the STAB bonus when adding to damage.

toxic-boost.d: When this Pokémon is hit by a poison-type attack, its next attack is rolled at advantage.

toxic-chain.d: When this Pokémon lands a hit against a target using a melee attack, the target must make a CON save DC 16, becoming badly poisoned on failure.

toxic-debris.d: When this Pokémon is damaged, it may use its reaction to emit toxic spikes. Each creature within 5ft of it must make a DEX save against a DC of this Pokémon's level + 2. On failure, the creature is poisoned.

trace.d: This Pokémon copies a random ability of an opponent when entering battle. The ability cannot be Flower Gift, Forecast, Illusion, Imposter, Multitype, Trace, Wonder Guard, or Zen Mode.

transformer.d: This Pokémon has a standard Normal form from which all stats are based, but may change forms as a bonus action to drastically change its abilities. The forms it can take are Attack, Defense, and Speed. In Attack form, it adds an additional +5 to its attack rolls, but all attacks against it has advantage. In Defense form, its AC increases by 3, but its attacks are rolled at disadvantage. If the activated move requires a save, the target(s) have advantage. In Speed form, it gains an additional attack action each turn, but the attack is done at disadvantage. If it is a move that requires a save, the target(s) have advantage.

transistor.d: When this Pokémon uses an electric-type move, it may roll the damage twice and choose either total.

triage.d: This Pokémon's healing or draining moves have a move time of 1 bonus action.

truant.d: This Pokémon cannot use the same move in back to back rounds.

turboblaze.d: This Pokémon’s moves completely ignore any ability that would hinder or prevent their effect on the target or the user's ability to hit the target.

unaware.d: When this Pokémon attacks an opponent, it ignores any stat changes the opponent has been affected with after the start of battle.

unburden.d: While this Pokémon is not holding an item, it gains 10 feet to its speed.

unnerve.d: Opponents in combat with this Pokémon cannot eat held berries.

unseen-fist.d: Melee attacks this Pokémon make may damage through the opponent's use of Protect or Detect.

vessel-of-ruin.d: Creatures within 60ft of this Pokémon which do not have a "* of Ruin" ability have -4 Wisdom score, to a minimum of 1. This effect does not stack, and the creature's Wisdom score is restored upon leaving the area of effect.

victory-star.d: While this Pokémon is in battle, all allied Pokémon add an additional +1 to their attack rolls.

vital-spirit.d: This Pokémon cannot be put to sleep.

volt-absorb.d: This Pokémon takes no damage from electricity or electric-type attacks. Instead, half of any electric damage done is absorbed, restoring the Pokémon's HP.

wandering-spirit.d: When this Pokémon is hit by a melee attack, one random ability of its attacker changes to Wandering Spirit for the remainder of the encounter, and the replaced ability replaces this Pokémon's Wandering Spirit ability.

water-absorb.d: This Pokémon takes no damage from water or water-type attacks. Instead, half of any water damage done is absorbed, restoring the Pokémon's HP.

water-bubble.d: This Pokémon is resistant to fire-type damage and immune to the burned condition.

water-compaction.d: After being damaged by a water-type move, any other damage dealt to this Pokémon until the beginning of its next turn is halved.

water-veil.d: This Pokémon is immune to burning.

weak-armor.d: When an attack hits this Pokémon, its speed increases by 5 feet, but its AC is temporarily reduced by 1 until the end of battle (for a maximum reduction of -5).

well-baked-body.d: This Pokémon takes no damage from fire or fire-type attacks. Instead, its AC increases by 2 until it takes damage or after 1 minute, whichever happens first. This effect does not stack with itself.

white-smoke.d: Other Pokémon's moves or abilities cannot lower this Pokémon stats.

wimp-out.d: When a damaging move causes this Pokémon to fall below 50% of its maximum HP, it MUST disengage and move up to its speed in a straight line towards its trainer as a free action. If this would put the Pokémon in range of switching out, it must do so as another free action if another Pokémon is available to replace it.

wind-power.d: After a wind move is activated that affects this pokemon, the number of damage dice used for its next electric-type attack doubles. Wind moves include Aeroblast, Air Cutter, Bleakwind Storm, Blizzard, Fairy Wind, Gust, Heat Wave, Hurricane, Icy Wind, Petal Blizzard, Sandsear Storm, Sandstorm, Springtide Storm, Tailwind, Twister, Whirlwind, and Wildbolt Storm.

wind-rider.d: This Pokémon is immune to damage dealt by wind moves. Additionally, this Pokémon's movement speed is double when moving with the wind's current direction, and halved when moving against the wind.

wonder-guard.d: This Pokémon is immune to damaging moves from types that are not in its vulnerabilities list. (Shedinja only. Cannot be passed or swapped)

wonder-skin.d: This Pokémon has advantage on all saving throws against being burned, frozen, poisoned, paralyzed, or asleep.

zen-mode.d: When Darmanitan is below 50% of its HP, it enters Zen Mode. In Zen Mode, Darmanitan changes into the form of a solid statue. Its type changes to Fire/Psychic, it gains +4 to its AC, and its STR and WIS ability scores are swapped.

zen-mode-galarian.d: When Galarian Darmanitan is below 50% of its HP, it enters Zen Mode. In Zen Mode, Galarian Darmanitan changes into the form of a flaming snowman. Its type changes to Ice/Fire, and its STR and DEX each increase by +2.

zero-to-hero.d: When a non-Pokémon ally of Palafin takes damage from a source outside that ally's control, Palafin may enter its Hero Form. In Hero Form, Palafin's size changes to Medium, its AC increases by 4, its base walking speed becomes 30ft, and each of its STR and DEX scores increase by 4, up to a maximum of 22. It may do this once per long rest. It reverts to normal form at the end of combat.

species.name: Bulbasaur
species.desc: The Seed Pokémon. It can go for days without eating a single morsel. In the bulb on its back, it stores energy.

species.name: Ivysaur
species.desc: The Seed Pokémon. The bud on its back grows by drawing energy. It gives off an aroma when it is ready to bloom.

species.name: Venusaur
species.desc: The Seed Pokémon. The flower on its back catches the sun’s rays. The sunlight is then absorbed and used for energy

species.name: Charmander
species.desc: The Lizard Pokémon. The flame at the tip of its tail makes a sound as it burns. You can only hear it in quiet places.

species.name: Charmeleon
species.desc: The Flame Pokémon. Tough fights could excite this Pokémon. When excited, it may breathe out bluish-white flames.

species.name: Charizard
species.desc: The Flame Pokémon. When this Pokémon expels a blast of superhot fire, the red flame at the tip of its tail burns more intensely.

species.name: Squirtle
species.desc: The Tiny Turtle Pokémon. Shoots water at prey while in the water. Withdraws into its shell when in danger.

species.name: Wartortle
species.desc: The Turtle Pokémon. When tapped on its head, this Pokémon will pull it in, but its tail will still stick out a little bit.

species.name: Blastoise
species.desc: The Shellfish Pokémon. Once it takes aim at its enemy, it blasts out water with even more force than a fire hose.

species.name: Caterpie
species.desc: The Worm Pokémon. If you touch the feeler on top of its head, it will release a horrible stink to protect itself.

species.name: Metapod
species.desc: The Cocoon Pokémon. Hardens its shell to protect itself. However, a large impact may cause it to pop out of its shell.

species.name: Butterfree
species.desc: The Butterfly Pokémon. Its wings, covered with poisonous powder, repel water. This allows it to fly in the rain.

species.name: Weedle
species.desc: The Hairy Bug Pokémon. Beware of the sharp stinger on its head. It hides in grass and bushes where it eats leaves.

species.name: Kakuna
species.desc: The Cocoon Pokémon. Able to move only slightly. When endangered, it may stick out its stinger and poison its enemy.

species.name: Beedrill
species.desc: The Poison Bee Pokémon. It has three poisonous stingers on its forelegs and its tail. They are used to jab its enemy repeatedly.

species.name: Pidgey
species.desc: The Tiny Bird Pokémon. Very docile. If attacked, it will often kick up sand to protect itself rather than fight back.

species.name: Pidgeotto
species.desc: The Bird Pokémon. This Pokémon is full of vitality. It constantly flies around its large territory in search of prey.

species.name: Pidgeot
species.desc: The Bird Pokémon. This Pokémon flies at Mach 2 speed, seeking prey. Its large talons are feared as wicked weapons.

species.name: Alolan Rattata
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. Night after night, they sneak into people’s homes seeking food. A massive outbreak of them has become an issue of public concern.

species.name: Rattata
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. Will chew on anything with its fangs. If you see one, you can be certain that 40 more live in the area.

species.name: Alolan Raticate
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. It has an incredibly greedy personality. Its nest is filled with so much food gathered by Rattata at its direction, it can’t possibly eat it all.

species.name: Raticate
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. Its hind feet are webbed. They act as flippers, so it can swim in rivers and hunt for prey.

species.name: Spearow
species.desc: The Tiny Bird Pokémon. Inept at flying high. However, it can fly around very fast to protect its territory.

species.name: Fearow
species.desc: The Beak Pokémon. A Pokémon that dates back many years. If it senses danger, it flies high and away, instantly.

species.name: Ekans
species.desc: The Snake Pokémon. The older it gets, the longer it grows. At night, it wraps its long body around tree branches to rest.

species.name: Arbok
species.desc: The Cobra Pokémon. The frightening patterns on its belly have been studied. Six variations have been confirmed.

species.name: Pikachu
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. This forest-dwelling Pokémon stores electricity in its cheeks, so you’ll feel a tingly shock if you touch it.

species.name: Alolan Raichu
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. It loves pancakes prepared with a secret Alolan recipe. Some wonder whether that recipe holds the key to this Pokémon’s evolution.

species.name: Raichu
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. When electricity builds up inside its body, it becomes feisty. It also glows in the dark.

species.name: Alolan Sandshrew
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. An ancient tradition of Alolan festivals, still carried on to this day, is a competition to slide Sandshrew across ice as far as one can.

species.name: Sandshrew
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. Its body is dry. When it gets cold at night, its hide is said to become coated with a fine dew.

species.name: Alolan Sandslash
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. It uses large, hooked claws to cut a path through deep snow as it runs. On snowy mountains, this Sandslash is faster than any other Pokémon.

species.name: Sandslash
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. It is skilled at slashing enemies with its claws. If broken, they start to grow back in a day.

species.name: Nidoran ♀
species.desc: The Poison Pin Pokémon. A mild-mannered Pokémon that does not like to fight. Beware—its small horn secretes venom.

species.name: Nidorina
species.desc: The Poison Pin Pokémon. When resting deep in its burrow, its barbs always retract. This is proof that it is relaxed.

species.name: Nidoqueen
species.desc: The Drill Pokémon. Tough scales cover the sturdy body of this Pokémon. It appears that the scales grow in cycles.

species.name: Nidoran ♂
species.desc: The Poison Pin Pokémon. Its large ears are always kept upright. If it senses danger, it will attack with a poisonous sting.

species.name: Nidorino
species.desc: The Poison Pin Pokémon. Its horn contains venom. If it stabs an enemy with the horn, the impact makes the poison leak out.

species.name: Nidoking
species.desc: The Drill Pokémon. Its steel-like hide adds to its powerful tackle. Its horns are so hard, they can pierce a diamond.

species.name: Clefairy
species.desc: The Fairy Pokémon. Adored for their cute looks and playfulness. They are thought to be rare, as they do not appear often.

species.name: Clefable
species.desc: The Fairy Pokémon. They appear to be very protective of their own world. It is a kind of fairy, rarely seen by people.

species.name: Alolan Vulpix
species.desc: The Fox Pokémon. If you carelessly approach it because it’s cute, the boss of the pack, Ninetales, will appear and freeze you.

species.name: Vulpix
species.desc: The Fox Pokémon. Both its fur and its tails are beautiful. As it grows, the tails split and form more tails.

species.name: Alolan Ninetales
species.desc: The Fox Pokémon. The reason it guides people all the way down to the mountain’s base is that it wants them to hurry up and leave.

species.name: Ninetales
species.desc: The Fox Pokémon. According to an enduring legend, nine noble saints were united and reincarnated as this Pokémon.

species.name: Jigglypuff
species.desc: The Balloon Pokémon. Uses its cute round eyes to enrapture its foe. It then sings a pleasing melody that lulls the foe to sleep.

species.name: Wigglytuff
species.desc: The Balloon Pokémon. Its body is very elastic. By inhaling deeply, it can continue to inflate itself without limit.

species.name: Zubat
species.desc: The Bat Pokémon. Emits ultrasonic cries while it flies. They act as a sonar used to check for objects in its way.

species.name: Golbat
species.desc: The Bat Pokémon. It attacks in a stealthy manner, without warning. Its sharp fangs are used to bite and to suck blood.

species.name: Oddish
species.desc: The Weed Pokémon. It may be mistaken for a clump of weeds. If you try to yank it out of the ground, it shrieks horribly.

species.name: Gloom
species.desc: The Weed Pokémon. Smells incredibly foul! However, around one out of a thousand people enjoy sniffing its nose-bending stink.

species.name: Vileplume
species.desc: The Flower Pokémon. Flaps its broad flower petals to scatter its poisonous pollen. The flapping sound is very loud.

species.name: Paras
species.desc: The Mushroom Pokémon. Burrows under the ground to gnaw on tree roots. The mushrooms on its back absorb most of the nutrition.

species.name: Parasect
species.desc: The Mushroom Pokémon. The bug host is drained of energy by the mushroom on its back. The mushroom appears to do all the thinking.

species.name: Venonat
species.desc: The Insect Pokémon. Its large eyes act as radar. In a bright place, you can see that they are clusters of many tiny eyes.

species.name: Venomoth
species.desc: The Poison Moth Pokémon. The powdery scales on its wings are hard to remove from skin. They also contain poison that leaks out on contact.

species.name: Alolan Diglett
species.desc: The Mole Pokémon. Its three hairs change shape depending on Diglett’s mood. When in communication with its comrades, its whiskers wobble to and fro.

species.name: Diglett
species.desc: The Mole Pokémon. It prefers dark places. It spends most of its time underground, though it may pop up in caves.

species.name: Alolan Dugtrio
species.desc: The Mole Pokémon. Its shining gold hair provides it with protection. It’s reputed that keeping any of its fallen hairs will bring bad luck.

species.name: Dugtrio
species.desc: The Mole Pokémon. A team of triplets that can burrow to a depth of 60 miles. It’s reported that this triggers an earthquake.

species.name: Alolan Meowth
species.desc: The Scratch Cat Pokémon. When its delicate pride is wounded, or when the gold coin on its forehead is dirtied, it flies into a hysterical rage.

species.name: Galarian Meowth
species.desc: The Scratch Cat Pokémon. Living with a savage, seafaring people has toughened this Pokémon's body so much that parts of it have turned to iron.

species.name: Meowth
species.desc: The Scratch Cat Pokémon. Appears to be more active at night. It loves round and shiny things. It can’t stop itself from picking them up.

species.name: Alolan Persian
species.desc: The Classy Cat Pokémon. It looks down on everyone other than itself. Its preferred tactics are sucker punches and blindside attacks.

species.name: Persian
species.desc: The Classy Cat Pokémon. The gem in its forehead glows on its own! It walks with all the grace and elegance of a proud queen.

species.name: Psyduck
species.desc: The Duck Pokémon. Always tormented by headaches. It uses psychic powers, but whether it intends to do so is not known.

species.name: Golduck
species.desc: The Duck Pokémon. Its long, slim limbs end in broad flippers. They are used for swimming gracefully in lakes.

species.name: Mankey
species.desc: The Pig Monkey Pokémon. An agile Pokémon that lives in trees. It angers easily and will not hesitate to attack anything.

species.name: Primeape
species.desc: The Pig Monkey Pokémon. It stops being angry only when nobody else is around. To view this moment is very difficult.
evTo: Annihilape (level 10, after using Rage Fist 10 times)

species.name: Growlithe
species.desc: The Puppy Pokémon. A Pokémon with a friendly nature. However, it will bark fiercely at anything invading its territory.

species.name: Hisuian Growlithe
species.desc: The Scout Pokémon. They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.

species.name: Arcanine
species.desc: The Legendary Pokémon. A legendary Pokémon in the East. Many people are charmed by the grace and beauty of its running.

species.name: Hisuian Arcanine
species.desc: The Legendary Pokémon. Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.

species.name: Poliwag
species.desc: The Tadpole Pokémon. The direction of the spiral on the belly differs by area. It is more adept at swimming than walking.

species.name: Poliwhirl
species.desc: The Tadpole Pokémon. Under attack, it uses its belly spiral to put the foe to sleep. It then makes its escape.

species.name: Poliwrath
species.desc: The Tadpole Pokémon. Swims powerfully using all the muscles in its body. It can even overtake world-class swimmers.

species.name: Abra
species.desc: The Psi Pokémon. Sleeps 18 hours a day. If it senses danger, it will teleport itself to safety even as it sleeps.

species.name: Kadabra
species.desc: The Psi Pokémon. Many odd things happen if this Pokémon is close by. For example, it makes clocks run backward.

species.name: Alakazam
species.desc: The Psi Pokémon. A Pokémon that can memorize anything. It never forgets what it learns—that’s why this Pokémon is smart.

species.name: Machop
species.desc: The Superpower Pokémon. Very powerful in spite of its small size. Its mastery of many types of martial arts makes it very tough.

species.name: Machoke
species.desc: The Superpower Pokémon. The belt around its waist holds back its energy. Without it, this Pokémon would be unstoppable.

species.name: Machamp
species.desc: The Superpower Pokémon. One arm alone can move mountains. Using all four arms, this Pokémon fires off awesome punches.

species.name: Bellsprout
species.desc: The Flower Pokémon. Prefers hot and humid places. It ensnares tiny bugs with its vines and devours them.

species.name: Weepinbell
species.desc: The Flycatcher Pokémon. When hungry, it swallows anything that moves. Its hapless prey is dissolved by strong acids.

species.name: Victreebel
species.desc: The Flycatcher Pokémon. Lures prey with the sweet aroma of honey. Swallowed whole, the prey is dissolved in a day, bones and all.

species.name: Tentacool
species.desc: The Jellyfish Pokémon. It can sometimes be found all dry and shriveled up on a beach. Toss it back into the sea to revive it.

species.name: Tentacruel
species.desc: The Jellyfish Pokémon. Its 80 tentacles can stretch and contract freely. They wrap around prey and weaken it with poison.

species.name: Alolan Geodude
species.desc: The Rock Pokémon. Its stone head is imbued with electricity and magnetism. If you carelessly step on one, you’ll be in for a painful shock.

species.name: Geodude
species.desc: The Rock Pokémon. Commonly found near mountain trails and the like. If you step on one by accident, it gets angry.

species.name: Alolan Graveler
species.desc: The Rock Pokémon. They eat rocks and often get into a scrap over them. The shock of Graveler smashing together causes a flash of light and a booming noise.

species.name: Graveler
species.desc: The Rock Pokémon. Often seen rolling down mountain trails. Obstacles are just things to roll straight over, not avoid.

species.name: Alolan Golem
species.desc: The Megaton Pokémon. Because it can’t fire boulders at a rapid pace, it’s been known to seize nearby Geodude and fire them from its back.

species.name: Golem
species.desc: The Megaton Pokémon. Once it sheds its skin, its body turns tender and whitish. Its hide hardens when it’s exposed to air.

species.name: Galarian Ponyta
species.desc: The Unique Horn Pokémon. Its small horn hides a healing power. With a few rubs from this Pokémon's horn, any slight wound you have will be healed.

species.name: Ponyta
species.desc: The Fire Horse Pokémon. Capable of jumping incredibly high. Its hooves and sturdy legs absorb the impact of a hard landing.

species.name: Galarian Rapidash
species.desc: The Unique Horn Pokémon. Fearless and proud, Rapidash uses Psychic powers stored in the flowing fur above its hooves to dash through the forest with ease.

species.name: Rapidash
species.desc: The Fire Horse Pokémon. Just loves to run. If it sees something faster than itself, it will give chase at top speed.

species.name: Galarian Slowpoke
species.desc: The Dopey Pokémon. Although this Pokémon is normally zoned out, its expression abruptly sharpens on occasion. The cause for this seems to lie in Slowpoke's diet.

species.name: Slowpoke
species.desc: The Dopey Pokémon. Incredibly slow and sluggish. It is quite content to loll about without worrying about the time.

species.name: Galarian Slowbro
species.desc: The Hermit Crab Pokémon. A Shellder bite set off a chemical reaction with the spices inside Slowbro's body, causing Slowbro to become a Poison-type Pokémon.

species.name: Slowbro
species.desc: The Hermit Crab Pokémon. Lives lazily by the sea. If the Shellder on its tail comes off, it becomes a Slowpoke again.

species.name: Magnemite
species.desc: The Magnet Pokémon. It is hatched with the ability to defy gravity. It floats while emitting powerful electromagnetic waves.

species.name: Magneton
species.desc: The Magnet Pokémon. Generates strange radio signals. It raises the temperature by 3.6 degrees Fahrenheit within 3,300 feet.

species.name: Farfetch'd
species.desc: The Wild Duck Pokémon. They live where reedy plants grow. Farfetch’d are rarely seen, so it’s thought their numbers are decreasing.

species.name: Galarian Farfetch'd
species.desc: The Wild Duck Pokémon. Farfetch'd always carries a leek that is twice as long and heavy as its own body and never lets go.
evTo: Sirfetch'd (level 8, after enduring a single battle where it lands three critical hits)

species.name: Doduo
species.desc: The Twin Bird Pokémon. Its short wings make flying difficult. Instead, this Pokémon runs at high speed on developed legs.

species.name: Dodrio
species.desc: The Triple Bird Pokémon. One of Doduo’s two heads splits to form a unique species. It runs close to 40 mph in prairies.

species.name: Seel
species.desc: The Sea Lion Pokémon. Loves freezing-cold conditions. Relishes swimming in a frigid climate of around 14 degrees Fahrenheit.

species.name: Dewgong
species.desc: The Sea Lion Pokémon. Its entire body is a snowy white. Unharmed by even intense cold, it swims powerfully in icy waters.

species.name: Alolan Grimer
species.desc: The Sludge Pokémon. Brought to Alola to solve the garbage problem, Grimer seems to relish any and all kinds of trash.

species.name: Grimer
species.desc: The Sludge Pokémon. Made of congealed sludge. It smells too putrid to touch. Even weeds won’t grow in its path.

species.name: Alolan Muk
species.desc: The Sludge Pokémon. While it’s unexpectedly quiet and friendly, if it’s not fed any trash for a while, it will smash its Trainer’s furnishings and eat up the fragments.

species.name: Muk
species.desc: The Sludge Pokémon. Smells so awful, it can cause fainting. Through degeneration of its nose, it lost its sense of smell.

species.name: Shellder
species.desc: The Bivalve Pokémon. The shell can withstand any attack. However, when it is open, the tender body is exposed.

species.name: Cloyster
species.desc: The Bivalve Pokémon. For protection, it uses its harder-than-diamond shell. It also shoots spikes from the shell.

species.name: Gastly
species.desc: The Gas Pokémon. Said to appear in decrepit, deserted buildings. It has no real shape, as it appears to be made of a gas.

species.name: Haunter
species.desc: The Gas Pokémon. By licking, it saps the victim’s life. It causes shaking that won’t stop until the victim’s demise.

species.name: Gengar
species.desc: The Shadow Pokémon. A Gengar is close by if you feel a sudden chill. It may be trying to lay a curse on you.

species.name: Onix
species.desc: The Rock Snake Pokémon. Burrows at high speed in search of food. The tunnels it leaves are used as homes by Diglett.

species.name: Drowzee
species.desc: The Hypnosis Pokémon. If you sleep by it all the time, it will sometimes show you dreams it had eaten in the past.

species.name: Hypno
species.desc: The Hypnosis Pokémon. Avoid eye contact if you come across one. It will try to put you to sleep by using its pendulum.

species.name: Krabby
species.desc: The River Crab Pokémon. Its pincers are superb weapons. They sometimes break off during battle, but they grow back fast.

species.name: Kingler
species.desc: The Pincer Pokémon. One claw grew massively and is as hard as steel. It has 10,000-horsepower strength. However, it is too heavy.

species.name: Hisuian Voltorb
species.desc: The Sphere Pokémon. An enigmatic Pokémon that happens to bear a resemblance to a Poké Ball. When excited, it discharges the electric current it has stored in its belly, then lets out a great, uproarious laugh.

species.name: Voltorb
species.desc: The Ball Pokémon. It is said to camouflage itself as a Poké Ball. It will self-destruct with very little stimulus.

species.name: Electrode
species.desc: The Ball Pokémon. Stores electrical energy inside its body. Even the slightest shock could trigger a huge explosion.

species.name: Hisuian Electrode
species.desc: The Sphere Pokémon. The tissue on the surface of its body is curiously similar in composition to an Apricorn. When irritated, this Pokémon lets loose an electric current equal to 20 lightning bolts.

species.name: Exeggcute
species.desc: The Egg Pokémon. The heads attract each other and spin around. There must be six heads for it to maintain balance.

species.name: Alolan Exeggutor
species.desc: The Coconut Pokémon. As it grew taller and taller, it outgrew its reliance on psychic powers, while within it awakened the power of the sleeping dragon.

species.name: Exeggutor
species.desc: The Coconut Pokémon. Its cries are very noisy. This is because each of the three heads thinks about whatever it likes.

species.name: Cubone
species.desc: The Lonely Pokémon. Wears the skull of its deceased mother. Its cries echo inside the skull and come out as a sad melody.

species.name: Alolan Marowak
species.desc: The Bone Keeper Pokémon. The bones it possesses were once its mother’s. Its mother’s regrets have become like a vengeful spirit protecting this Pokémon.

species.name: Marowak
species.desc: The Bone Keeper Pokémon. Small and weak, this Pokémon is adept with its bone club. It has grown more vicious over the ages.

species.name: Hitmonlee
species.desc: The Kicking Pokémon. When kicking, the sole of its foot turns as hard as a diamond on impact and destroys its enemy.

species.name: Hitmonchan
species.desc: The Punching Pokémon. Punches in corkscrew fashion. It can punch its way through a concrete wall like a drill.

species.name: Lickitung
species.desc: The Licking Pokémon. Its tongue spans almost seven feet and moves more freely than its forelegs. Its licks can cause paralysis.

species.name: Koffing
species.desc: The Poison Gas Pokémon. In hot places, its internal gases could expand and explode without any warning. Be very careful!
evTo: Galarian Weezing (level 9, while in a region with significant anthropogenic pollution)

species.name: Galarian Weezing
species.desc: The Poison Gas Pokémon. This Pokémon consumes particles that contaminate the air. Instead of leaving droppings, it expels clean air.

species.name: Weezing
species.desc: The Poison Gas Pokémon. This Pokémon lives and grows by absorbing poison gas, dust, and germs that exist inside garbage.

species.name: Rhyhorn
species.desc: The Spikes Pokémon. A Pokémon with a one-track mind. Once it charges, it won’t stop running until it falls asleep.

species.name: Rhydon
species.desc: The Drill Pokémon. Its brain developed when it began walking on its hind legs. Its armor-like hide even repels molten lava.

species.name: Chansey
species.desc: The Egg Pokémon. A gentle and kindhearted Pokémon that shares its nutritious eggs if it sees an injured Pokémon.

species.name: Tangela
species.desc: The Vine Pokémon. Its identity is obscured by masses of thick blue vines. The vines are said to never stop growing.

species.name: Kangaskhan
species.desc: The Parent Pokémon. Raises its young in its belly pouch. Won’t run from any fight to keep its young protected.

species.name: Horsea
species.desc: The Dragon Pokémon. If it senses any danger, it will vigorously spray water or a special type of ink from its mouth.

species.name: Seadra
species.desc: The Dragon Pokémon. Touching the back fin causes numbness. It hooks its tail to coral to stay in place while sleeping.

species.name: Goldeen
species.desc: The Goldfish Pokémon. When it is time for them to lay eggs, they can be seen swimming up rivers and falls in large groups.

species.name: Seaking
species.desc: The Goldfish Pokémon. It is the male’s job to make a nest by carving out boulders in a stream using the horn on its head.

species.name: Staryu
species.desc: The Star Shape Pokémon. As long as the center section is unharmed, this Pokémon can grow back fully even if it is chopped to bits.

species.name: Starmie
species.desc: The Mysterious Pokémon. The center section is named the core. People think it is communicating when it glows in seven colors.

species.name: Galarian Mr. Mime
species.desc: The Dancing Pokémon. Its talent is tap-dancing. It can also manipulate temperatures to create a floor of ice, which this Pokémon can kick up to use as a barrier.

species.name: Mr. Mime
species.desc: The Barrier Pokémon. Always practicing its pantomime act. It makes enemies believe something exists that really doesn’t.

species.name: Scyther
species.desc: The Mantis Pokémon. Leaps out of tall grass and slices prey with its scythes. The movement looks like that of a ninja.

species.name: Jynx
species.desc: The Human Shape Pokémon. Appears to move to a rhythm of its own, as if it were dancing. It wiggles its hips as it walks.

species.name: Electabuzz
species.desc: The Electric Pokémon. If a major power outage occurs, it is certain that this Pokémon has eaten electricity at a power plant.

species.name: Magmar
species.desc: The Spitfire Pokémon. Born in an active volcano. Its body is always cloaked in flames, so it looks like a big ball of fire.

species.name: Pinsir
species.desc: The Stag Beetle Pokémon. Grips its prey in its pincers and squeezes hard! It can’t move if it’s cold out, so it lives in warm places.

species.name: Paldean Tauros (Aqua Breed)
species.desc: The Wild Bull Pokémon. This Pokémon blasts water from holes on the tips of its horns—the high-pressure jets pierce right through Tauros’s enemies.

species.name: Paldean Tauros (Blaze Breed)
species.desc: The Wild Bull Pokémon. When heated by fire energy, its horns can get hotter than 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit. Those gored by them will suffer both wounds and burns.

species.name: Paldean Tauros (Combat Breed)
species.desc: The Wild Bull Pokémon. This Pokémon has a muscular body and excels at close-quarters combat. It uses its short horns to strike the opponent’s weak spots.

species.name: Tauros
species.desc: The Wild Bull Pokémon. A rowdy Pokémon with a lot of stamina. Once running, it won’t stop until it hits something.

species.name: Magikarp
species.desc: The Fish Pokémon. Famous for being very unreliable. It can be found swimming in seas, lakes, rivers, and shallow puddles.

species.name: Gyarados
species.desc: The Atrocious Pokémon. Brutally vicious and enormously destructive. Known for totally destroying cities in ancient times.

species.name: Lapras
species.desc: The Transport Pokémon. A gentle soul that can understand human speech. It can ferry people across the sea on its back.

species.name: Ditto
species.desc: The Transform Pokémon. When it spots an enemy, its body transfigures into an almost-perfect copy of its opponent.

species.name: Eevee
species.desc: The Evolution Pokémon. Eevee’s genes are the key to solving the mysteries of Pokémon evolution.
evTo: Sylveon (level 8, loyalty 2, knowing a fairy-type move)

species.name: Vaporeon
species.desc: The Bubble Jet Pokémon. Its cell structure is similar to water molecules. It melts into the water and becomes invisible.

species.name: Jolteon
species.desc: The Lightning Pokémon. A sensitive Pokémon that easily becomes sad or angry. Every time its mood changes, it charges power.

species.name: Flareon
species.desc: The Flame Pokémon. It has a flame chamber inside its body. It inhales, then breathes out fire that is over 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.

species.name: Porygon
species.desc: The Virtual Pokémon. The only Pokémon that people anticipate can fly into space. None has managed the feat yet, however.

species.name: Omanyte
species.desc: The Spiral Pokémon. An ancient Pokémon that was recovered from a fossil. It swam by cleverly twisting its 10 tentacles about.

species.name: Omastar
species.desc: The Spiral Pokémon. Its sharp beak rings its mouth. Its shell was too big for it to move freely, so it became extinct.

species.name: Kabuto
species.desc: The Shellfish Pokémon. A Pokémon that was recovered from a fossil. It used the eyes on its back while hiding on the seafloor.

species.name: Kabutops
species.desc: The Shellfish Pokémon. A slim and fast swimmer. It sliced its prey with its sharp sickles and drank the body fluids.

species.name: Aerodactyl
species.desc: The Fossil Pokémon. A savage Pokémon that died out in ancient times. It was resurrected using DNA taken from amber.

species.name: Snorlax
species.desc: The Sleeping Pokémon. Will eat anything, even if the food happens to be a little moldy. It never gets an upset stomach.

species.name: Articuno
species.desc: The Freeze Pokémon. A legendary bird Pokémon. It freezes water that is contained in winter air and makes it snow.

species.name: Galarian Articuno
species.desc: The Cruel Pokémon. Its feather-like blades are composed of psychic energy and can shear through thick iron sheets as if they were paper.

species.name: Galarian Zapdos
species.desc: The Strong Legs Pokémon. One kick from its powerful legs will pulverize a dump truck. Supposedly, this Pokémon runs through the mountains at over 180 mph.

species.name: Zapdos
species.desc: The Electric Pokémon. This legendary bird Pokémon is said to appear when the sky turns dark and lightning showers down.

species.name: Galarian Moltres
species.desc: The Malevolent Pokémon. This Pokémon’s sinister, flame-like aura will consume the spirit of any creature it hits. Victims become burned-out shadows of themselves.

species.name: Moltres
species.desc: The Flame Pokémon. A legendary bird Pokémon. As it flaps its flaming wings, even the night sky will turn red.

species.name: Dratini
species.desc: The Dragon Pokémon. Long thought to be a myth, this Pokémon’s existence was only recently confirmed by a fisherman who caught one.

species.name: Dragonair
species.desc: The Dragon Pokémon. According to a witness, its body was surrounded by a strange aura that gave it a mystical look.

species.name: Dragonite
species.desc: The Dragon Pokémon. It is said that this Pokémon lives somewhere in the sea and that it flies. However, these are only rumors.

species.name: Mewtwo
species.desc: The Genetic Pokémon. Its DNA is almost the same as Mew’s. However, its size and disposition are vastly different.

species.name: Mew
species.desc: The New Species Pokémon. When viewed through a microscope, this Pokémon’s short, fine, delicate hair can be seen.

species.name: Chikorita
species.desc: The Leaf Pokémon. In battle, Chikorita waves its leaf around to keep the foe at bay. However, a sweet fragrance also wafts from the leaf, becalming the battling Pokémon and creating a cozy, friendly atmosphere all around.

species.name: Bayleef
species.desc: The Leaf Pokémon. Bayleef's neck is ringed by curled-up leaves. Inside each tubular leaf is a small shoot of a tree. The fragrance of this shoot makes people peppy.

species.name: Meganium
species.desc: The Herb Pokémon. The fragrance of Meganium's flower soothes and calms emotions. In battle, this Pokémon gives off more of its becalming scent to blunt the foe's fighting spirit.

species.name: Cyndaquil
species.desc: The Fire Mouse Pokémon. Cyndaquil protects itself by flaring up the flames on its back. The flames are vigorous if the Pokémon is angry. However, if it is tired, the flames splutter fitfully with incomplete combustion.

species.name: Quilava
species.desc: The Volcano Pokémon. Quilava keeps its foes at bay with the intensity of its flames and gusts of superheated air. This Pokémon applies its outstanding nimbleness to dodge attacks even while scorching the foe with flames.

species.name: Hisuian Typhlosion
species.desc: The Ghost Flame Pokémon. Said to purify lost, forsaken souls with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. I believe its form has been influenced by the energy of the sacred mountain towering at Hisui’s center.

species.name: Typhlosion
species.desc: The Volcano Pokémon. Typhlosion obscures itself behind a shimmering heat haze that it creates using its intensely hot flames. This Pokémon creates blazing explosive blasts that burn everything to cinders.

species.name: Totodile
species.desc: The Big Jaw Pokémon. Despite the smallness of its body, Totodile's jaws are very powerful. While the Pokémon may think it is just playfully nipping, its bite has enough power to cause serious injury.

species.name: Croconaw
