species.desc: The Mole Pokémon. It makes its way swiftly through the soil by putting both claws together and rotating at high speed.

species.name: Excadrill
species.desc: The Subterrene Pokémon. More than 300 feet below the surface, they build mazelike nests. Their activity can be destructive to subway tunnels.

species.name: Audino
species.desc: The Hearing Pokémon. Its auditory sense is astounding. It has a radarlike ability to understand its surroundings through slight sounds.

species.name: Timburr
species.desc: The Muscular Pokémon. These Pokémon appear at building sites and help out with construction. They always carry squared logs.

species.name: Gurdurr
species.desc: The Muscular Pokémon. They strengthen their bodies by carrying steel beams. They show off their big muscles to their friends.

species.name: Conkeldurr
species.desc: The Muscular Pokémon. They use concrete pillars as walking canes. They know moves that enable them to swing the pillars freely in battle.

species.name: Tympole
species.desc: The Tadpole Pokémon. By vibrating its cheeks, it emits sound waves imperceptible to humans. It uses the rhythm of these sounds to talk.

species.name: Palpitoad
species.desc: The Vibration Pokémon. It lives in the water and on land. It uses its long, sticky tongue to capture prey.

species.name: Seismitoad
species.desc: The Vibration Pokémon. It increases the power of its punches by vibrating the bumps on its fists. It can turn a boulder to rubble with one punch.

species.name: Throh
species.desc: The Judo Pokémon. When they encounter foes bigger than themselves, they try to throw them. They always travel in packs of five.

species.name: Sawk
species.desc: The Karate Pokémon. Tying their belts gets them pumped and makes their punches more destructive. Disturbing their training angers them.

species.name: Sewaddle
species.desc: The Sewing Pokémon. This Pokémon makes clothes for itself. It chews up leaves and sews them with sticky thread extruded from its mouth.

species.name: Swadloon
species.desc: The Leaf-Wrapped Pokémon. It protects itself from the cold by wrapping up in leaves. It stays on the move, eating leaves in forests.

species.name: Leavanny
species.desc: The Nurturing Pokémon. It keeps its eggs warm with heat from fermenting leaves. It also uses leaves to make warm wrappings for Sewaddle.

species.name: Venipede
species.desc: The Centipede Pokémon. It discovers what is going on around it by using the feelers on its head and tail. It is brutally aggressive.

species.name: Whirlipede
species.desc: The Curlipede Pokémon. It is usually motionless, but when attacked, it rotates at high speed and then crashes into its opponent.

species.name: Scolipede
species.desc: The Megapede Pokémon. Highly aggressive, it uses the claws near its neck to dig into its opponents and poison them.

species.name: Cottonee
species.desc: The Cotton Puff Pokémon. They go wherever the wind takes them. On rainy days, their bodies are heavier, so they take shelter beneath big trees.

species.name: Whimsicott
species.desc: The Windveiled Pokémon. Riding whirlwinds, they appear. These Pokémon sneak through gaps into houses and cause all sorts of mischief.

species.name: Petilil
species.desc: The Bulb Pokémon. Since they prefer moist, nutrient-rich soil, the areas where Petilil live are known to be good for growing plants.

species.name: Hisuian Lilligant
species.desc: The Spinning Pokémon. I suspect that its well-developed legs are the result of a life spent on mountains covered in deep snow. The scent it exudes from its flower crown heartens those in proximity.

species.name: Lilligant
species.desc: The Flowering Pokémon. The fragrance of the garland on its head has a relaxing effect. It withers if a Trainer does not take good care of it.

species.name: Basculin (Blue)
species.desc: The Hostile Pokémon. Red and blue Basculin usually do not get along, but sometimes members of one school mingle with the other's school.
evTo: Basculegion ♂ (level 10, male only, after fainting to damage taken from a melee attack)
Basculegion ♀ (level 10, female only, after fainting to damage taken from a melee attack)

species.name: Basculin (Red)
species.desc: The Hostile Pokémon. Red and blue Basculin usually do not get along, but sometimes members of one school mingle with the other's school.
evTo: Basculegion ♂ (level 10, male only, after fainting from recoil damage)
Basculegion ♀ (level 10, female only, after fainting from recoil damage)

species.name: Basculin (White)
species.desc: The Mellow Pokémon. It differs from other Basculin in several respects, including demeanor. This one is gentle.
evTo: Basculegion ♂ (level 10, male only, after fainting from recoil damage)
Basculegion ♀ (level 10, female only, after fainting from recoil damage)

species.name: Sandile
species.desc: The Desert Croc Pokémon. It moves along below the sand's surface, except for its nose and eyes. A dark membrane shields its eyes from the sun.

species.name: Krokorok
species.desc: The Desert Croc Pokémon. The special membrane covering its eyes can sense the heat of objects, so it can see its surroundings even in darkness.

species.name: Krookodile
species.desc: The Intimidation Pokémon. It can expand the focus of its eyes, enabling it to see objects in the far distance as if it were using binoculars.

species.name: Darumaka
species.desc: The Zen Charm Pokémon. Darumaka's droppings are hot, so people used to put them in their clothes to keep themselves warm.

species.name: Galarian Darumaka
species.desc: The Zen Charm Pokémon. It lived in snowy areas for so long that its fire sac cooled off and atrophied. It now has an organ that generates cold instead.

species.name: Darmanitan
species.desc: The Blazing Pokémon. When weakened in battle, it transforms into a stone statue. Then it sharpens its mind and fights on mentally.

species.name: Galarian Darmanitan
species.desc: The Zen Mode Pokémon. On days when blizzards blow through, it comes down to where people live. It stashes food in the snowball on its head, taking it home for later.

species.name: Maractus
species.desc: The Cactus Pokémon. Arid regions are their habitat. They move rhythmically, making a sound similar to maracas.

species.name: Dwebble
species.desc: The Rock Inn Pokémon. It makes a hole in a suitable rock. If that rock breaks, the Pokémon remains agitated until it locates a replacement.

species.name: Crustle
species.desc: The Stone Home Pokémon. It possesses legs of enormous strength, enabling it to carry heavy slabs for many days, even when crossing arid land.

species.name: Scraggy
species.desc: The Shedding Pokémon. It immediately headbutts anyone that makes eye contact with it. Its skull is massively thick.

species.name: Scrafty
species.desc: The Hoodlum Pokémon. It can smash concrete blocks with its kicking attacks. The one with the biggest crest is the group leader.

species.name: Sigilyph
species.desc: The Avianoid Pokémon. The guardians of an ancient city, they use their psychic power to attack enemies that invade their territory.

species.name: Galarian Yamask
species.desc: The Spirit Pokémon. A clay slab with cursed engravings took possession of a Yamask. The slab is said to be absorbing the Yamask's dark power.

species.name: Yamask
species.desc: The Spirit Pokémon. These Pokémon arose from the spirits of people interred in graves in past ages. Each retains memories of its former life.

species.name: Cofagrigus
species.desc: The Coffin Pokémon. They pretend to be elaborate coffins to teach lessons to grave robbers. Their bodies are covered in pure gold.

species.name: Tirtouga
species.desc: The Prototurtle Pokémon. About 100 million years ago, these Pokémon swam in oceans. It is thought they also went on land to attack prey.

species.name: Carracosta
species.desc: The Prototurtle Pokémon. Incredible jaw strength enables them to chew up steel beams and rocks along with their prey.

species.name: Archen
species.desc: The First Bird Pokémon. Revived from a fossil, this Pokémon is thought to be the ancestor of all bird Pokémon.

species.name: Archeops
species.desc: The First Bird Pokémon. It runs better than it flies. It catches prey by running at speeds comparable to those of an automobile.

species.name: Trubbish
species.desc: The Trash Bag Pokémon. The combination of garbage bags and industrial waste caused the chemical reaction that created this Pokémon.

species.name: Garbodor
species.desc: The Trash Heap Pokémon. They absorb garbage and make it part of their bodies. They shoot a poisonous liquid from their right-hand fingertips.

species.name: Hisuian Zorua
species.desc: The Spiteful Fox Pokémon. A once-departed soul, returned to life in Hisui. Derives power from resentment, which rises as energy atop its head and takes on the forms of foes. In this way, Zorua vents lingering malice.

species.name: Zorua
species.desc: The Tricky Fox Pokémon. To protect themselves from danger, they hide their true identities by transforming into people and Pokémon.

species.name: Hisuian Zoroark
species.desc: The Baneful Fox Pokémon. With its disheveled white fur, it looks like an embodiment of death. Heedless of its own safety, Zoroark attacks its nemeses with a bitter energy so intense, it lacerates Zoroark’s own body.

species.name: Zoroark
species.desc: The Illusion Fox Pokémon. Each has the ability to fool a large group of people simultaneously. They protect their lair with illusory scenery.

species.name: Minccino
species.desc: The Chinchilla Pokémon. These Pokémon prefer a tidy habitat. They are always sweeping and dusting, using their tails as brooms.

species.name: Cinccino
species.desc: The Scarf Pokémon. Their white fur feels amazing to touch. Their fur repels dust and prevents static electricity from building up.

species.name: Gothita
species.desc: The Fixation Pokémon. They intently observe both Trainers and Pokémon. Apparently, they are looking at something that only Gothita can see.

species.name: Gothorita
species.desc: The Manipulate Pokémon. Starlight is the source of their power. At night, they mark star positions by using psychic power to float stones.

species.name: Gothitelle
species.desc: The Astral Body Pokémon. They can predict the future from the placement and movement of the stars. They can see Trainers' life spans.

species.name: Solosis
species.desc: The Cell Pokémon. Because their bodies are enveloped in a special liquid, they can survive in any environment.

species.name: Duosion
species.desc: The Mitosis Pokémon. When their brains, now divided in two, are thinking the same thoughts, these Pokémon exhibit their maximum power.

species.name: Reuniclus
species.desc: The Multiplying Pokémon. These remarkably intelligent Pokémon fight by controlling arms that can grip with rock-crushing power.

species.name: Ducklett
species.desc: The Water Bird Pokémon. When attacked, it uses its feathers to splash water, escaping under cover of the spray.

species.name: Swanna
species.desc: The White Bird Pokémon. It administers sharp, powerful pecks with its bill. It whips its long neck to deliver forceful repeated strikes.

species.name: Vanillite
species.desc: The Fresh Snow Pokémon. This Pokémon formed from icicles bathed in energy from the morning sun. It sleeps buried in snow.

species.name: Vanillish
species.desc: The Icy Snow Pokémon. It conceals itself from enemy eyes by creating many small ice particles and hiding among them.

species.name: Vanilluxe
species.desc: The Snowstorm Pokémon. If both heads get angry simultaneously, this Pokémon expels a blizzard, burying everything in snow.

species.name: Deerling
species.desc: The Season Pokémon. The turning of the seasons changes the color and scent of this Pokémon's fur. People use it to mark the seasons.

species.name: Sawsbuck
species.desc: The Season Pokémon. The plants growing on its horns change according to the season. The leaders of the herd possess magnificent horns.

species.name: Emolga
species.desc: The Sky Squirrel Pokémon. They live on treetops and glide using the inside of a cape-like membrane while discharging electricity.

species.name: Karrablast
species.desc: The Clamping Pokémon. When they feel threatened, they spit an acidic liquid to drive attackers away. This Pokémon targets Shelmet.
evTo: Escavalier (level 8, while in the presence of a Shelmet)

species.name: Escavalier
species.desc: The Cavalry Pokémon. These Pokémon evolve by wearing the shell covering of a Shelmet. The steel armor protects their whole body.

species.name: Foongus
species.desc: The Mushroom Pokémon. For some reason, this Pokémon resembles a Poké Ball. They release poison spores to repel those who try to catch them.

species.name: Amoonguss
species.desc: The Mushroom Pokémon. They show off their Poké Ball caps to lure prey, but very few Pokémon are fooled by this.

species.name: Frillish
species.desc: The Floating Pokémon. They paralyze prey with poison, then drag them down to their lairs, five miles below the surface.

species.name: Jellicent
species.desc: The Floating Pokémon. They propel themselves by expelling absorbed seawater from their bodies. Their favorite food is life energy.

species.name: Alomomola
species.desc: The Caring Pokémon. Floating in the open sea is how they live. When they find a wounded Pokémon, they embrace it and bring it to shore.

species.name: Joltik
species.desc: The Attaching Pokémon. They attach themselves to large-bodied Pokémon and absorb static electricity, which they store in an electric pouch.

species.name: Galvantula
species.desc: The EleSpider Pokémon. They employ an electrically charged web to trap their prey. While it is immobilized by shock, they leisurely consume it.

species.name: Ferroseed
species.desc: The Thorn Seed Pokémon. They stick their spikes into cave walls and absorb the minerals they find in the rock.

species.name: Ferrothorn
species.desc: The Thorn Pod Pokémon. They attach themselves to cave ceilings, firing steel spikes at targets passing beneath them.

species.name: Klink
species.desc: The Gear Pokémon. Interlocking two bodies and spinning around generates the energy they need to live.

species.name: Klang
species.desc: The Gear Pokémon. Spinning minigears are rotated at high speed and repeatedly fired away. It is dangerous if the gears don't return.

species.name: Klinklang
species.desc: The Gear Pokémon. The gear with the red core is rotated at high speed for a rapid energy charge.

species.name: Tynamo
species.desc: The EleFish Pokémon. These Pokémon move in schools. They have an electricity-generating organ, so they discharge electricity if in danger.

species.name: Eelektrik
species.desc: The EleFish Pokémon. These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.

species.name: Eelektross
species.desc: The EleFish Pokémon. With their sucker mouths, they suck in prey. Then they use their fangs to shock the prey with electricity.

species.name: Elgyem
species.desc: The Cerebral Pokémon. This Pokémon had never been seen until it appeared from far in the desert 50 years ago.

species.name: Beheeyem
species.desc: The Cerebral Pokémon. It uses psychic power to control an opponent's brain and tamper with its memories.

species.name: Litwick
species.desc: The Candle Pokémon. While shining a light and pretending to be a guide, it leeches off the life force of any who follow it.

species.name: Lampent
species.desc: The Lamp Pokémon. It arrives near the moment of death and steals spirit from the body.

species.name: Chandelure
species.desc: The Luring Pokémon. Being consumed in Chandelure's flame burns up the spirit, leaving the body behind.

species.name: Axew
species.desc: The Tusk Pokémon. They mark their territory by leaving gashes in trees with their tusks. If a tusk breaks, a new one grows in quickly.

species.name: Fraxure
species.desc: The Axe Jaw Pokémon. Their tusks can shatter rocks. Territory battles between Fraxure can be intensely violent.

species.name: Haxorus
species.desc: The Axe Jaw Pokémon. Their sturdy tusks will stay sharp even if used to cut steel beams. These Pokémon are covered in hard armor.

species.name: Cubchoo
species.desc: The Chill Pokémon. Its nose is always running. It sniffs the snot back up because the mucus provides the raw material for its moves.

species.name: Beartic
species.desc: The Freezing Pokémon. It freezes its breath to create fangs and claws of ice to fight with. Cold northern areas are its habitat.

species.name: Cryogonal
species.desc: The Crystallizing Pokémon. They are born in snow clouds. They use chains made of ice crystals to capture prey.

species.name: Shelmet
species.desc: The Snail Pokémon. It evolves when bathed in an electric-like energy along with Karrablast. The reason is still unknown.
evTo: Accelgor (level 10, while in the presence of a Karrablast)

species.name: Accelgor
species.desc: The Shell Out Pokémon. Having removed its heavy shell, it becomes very light and can fight with ninja-like movements.

species.name: Galarian Stunfisk
species.desc: The Trap Pokémon. Its conspicuous lips lure prey in as it lies in wait in the mud. When prey gets close, Stunfisk clamps its jagged steel fins down on them.

species.name: Stunfisk
species.desc: The Trap Pokémon. It conceals itself in the mud of the seashore. Then it waits. When prey touch it, it delivers a jolt of electricity.

species.name: Mienfoo
species.desc: The Martial Arts Pokémon. They have mastered elegant combos. As they concentrate, their battle moves become swifter and more precise.

species.name: Mienshao
species.desc: The Martial Arts Pokémon. They use the long fur on their arms as a whip to strike their opponents.

species.name: Druddigon
species.desc: The Cave Pokémon. It races through narrow caves, using its sharp claws to catch prey. The skin on its face is harder than a rock.

species.name: Golett
species.desc: The Automaton Pokémon. These Pokémon are thought to have been created by the science of an ancient and mysterious civilization.

species.name: Golurk
species.desc: The Automaton Pokémon. It is said that Golurk were ordered to protect people and Pokémon by the ancient people who made them.

species.name: Pawniard
species.desc: The Sharp Blade Pokémon. They fight at Bisharp's command. They cling to their prey and inflict damage by sinking their blades into it.

species.name: Bisharp
species.desc: The Sword Blade Pokémon. Bisharp pursues prey in the company of a large group of Pawniard. Then Bisharp finishes off the prey.
evTo: Kingambit (level 15, after defeating an evolution of Pawniard that's holding a Leader's Crest one-on-one, while itself holding a Leader's Crest)

species.name: Bouffalant
species.desc: The Bash Buffalo Pokémon. They charge wildly and headbutt everything. Their headbutts have enough destructive force to derail a train.

species.name: Rufflet
species.desc: The Eaglet Pokémon. They will challenge anything, even strong opponents, without fear. Their frequent fights help them become stronger.

species.name: Braviary
species.desc: The Valiant Pokémon. The more scars they have, the more respect these brave soldiers of the sky get from their peers.

species.name: Hisuian Braviary
species.desc: The Battle Cry Pokémon. Screaming a bloodcurdling battle cry, this huge and ferocious bird Pokémon goes out on the hunt. It blasts lakes with shock waves, then scoops up any prey that float to the water’s surface.

species.name: Vullaby
species.desc: The Diapered Pokémon. They tend to guard their posteriors with suitable bones they have found. They pursue weak Pokémon.

species.name: Mandibuzz
species.desc: The Bone Vulture Pokémon. Watching from the sky, they swoop to strike weakened Pokémon on the ground. They decorate themselves with bones.

species.name: Heatmor
species.desc: The Anteater Pokémon. Using their very hot, flame-covered tongues, they burn through Durant's steel bodies and consume their insides.

species.name: Durant
species.desc: The Iron Ant Pokémon. Durant dig nests in mountains. They build their complicated, interconnected tunnels into mazes.

species.name: Deino
species.desc: The Irate Pokémon. They cannot see, so they tackle and bite to learn about their surroundings. Their bodies are covered in wounds.

species.name: Zweilous
species.desc: The Hostile Pokémon. Since their two heads do not get along and compete with each other for food, they always eat too much.

species.name: Hydreigon
species.desc: The Brutal Pokémon. The heads on their arms do not have brains. They use all three heads to consume and destroy everything.

species.name: Larvesta
species.desc: The Torch Pokémon. The base of volcanoes is where they make their homes. They shoot fire from their five horns to repel attacking enemies.

species.name: Volcarona
species.desc: The Sun Pokémon. A sea of fire engulfs the surroundings of their battles, since they use their six wings to scatter their ember scales.

species.name: Cobalion
species.desc: The Iron Will Pokémon. It has a body and heart of steel. Its glare is sufficient to make even an unruly Pokémon obey it.

species.name: Terrakion
species.desc: The Cavern Pokémon. Its charge is strong enough to break through a giant castle wall in one blow. This Pokémon is spoken of in legends.

species.name: Virizion
species.desc: The Grassland Pokémon. Its head sprouts horns as sharp as blades. Using whirlwind-like movements, it confounds and swiftly cuts opponents.

species.name: Tornadus (Incarnate)
species.desc: The Cyclone Pokémon. Tornadus expels massive energy from its tail, causing severe storms. Its power is great enough to blow houses away.

species.name: Tornadus (Therian)
species.desc: The Cyclone Pokémon. Tornadus expels massive energy from its tail, causing severe storms. Its power is great enough to blow houses away.

species.name: Thundurus (Incarnate)
species.desc: The Bolt Strike Pokémon. The spikes on its tail discharge immense bolts of lightning. It flies around the Unova region firing off lightning bolts.

species.name: Thundurus (Therian)
species.desc: The Bolt Strike Pokémon. The spikes on its tail discharge immense bolts of lightning. It flies around the Unova region firing off lightning bolts.

species.name: Reshiram
species.desc: The Vast White Pokémon. When Reshiram's tail flares, the heat energy moves the atmosphere and changes the world's weather.

species.name: Zekrom
species.desc: The Deep Black Pokémon. This Pokémon appears in legends. In its tail, it has a giant generator that creates electricity.

species.name: Landorus (Incarnate)
species.desc: The Abundance Pokémon. The energy that comes pouring from its tail increases the nutrition in the soil, making crops grow to great size.

species.name: Landorus (Therian)
species.desc: The Abundance Pokémon. The energy that comes pouring from its tail increases the nutrition in the soil, making crops grow to great size.

species.name: Black Kyurem
species.desc: The Boundary Pokémon. It can produce ultracold air. Its body is frozen.

species.name: Kyurem
species.desc: The Boundary Pokémon. It can produce ultracold air. Its body is frozen.

species.name: White Kyurem
species.desc: The Boundary Pokémon. It can produce ultracold air. Its body is frozen.

species.name: Keldeo
species.desc: The Colt Pokémon. It crosses the world, running over the surfaces of oceans and rivers. It appears at scenic waterfronts.

species.name: Meloetta - Aria
species.desc: The Melody Pokémon. Many famous songs have been inspired by the melodies that Meloetta plays.

species.name: Meloetta - Pirouette
species.desc: The Melody Pokémon. Many famous songs have been inspired by the melodies that Meloetta plays.

species.name: Genesect
species.desc: The Paleozoic Pokémon. This ancient bug Pokémon was altered by Team Plasma. They upgraded the cannon on its back.

species.name: Chespin
species.desc: The Spiny Nut Pokémon. The quills on its head are usually soft. When it flexes them, the points become so hard and sharp that they can pierce rock.

species.name: Quilladin
species.desc: The Spiny Armor Pokémon. It relies on its sturdy shell to deflect predators' attacks. It counterattacks with its sharp quills.

species.name: Chesnaught
species.desc: The Spiny Armor Pokémon. Its Tackle is forceful enough to flip a 50-ton tank. It shields its allies from danger with its own body.

species.name: Fennekin
species.desc: The Fox Pokémon. Eating a twig fills it with energy, and its roomy ears give vent to air hotter than 390 degrees Fahrenheit.

species.name: Braixen
species.desc: The Fox Pokémon. It has a twig stuck in its tail. With friction from its tail fur, it sets the twig on fire and launches into battle.

species.name: Delphox
species.desc: The Fox Pokémon. It gazes into the flame at the tip of its branch to achieve a focused state, which allows it to see into the future.

species.name: Froakie
species.desc: The Bubble Frog Pokémon. It secretes flexible bubbles from its chest and back. The bubbles reduce the damage it would otherwise take when attacked.

species.name: Frogadier
species.desc: The Bubble Frog Pokémon. It can throw bubble-covered pebbles with precise control, hitting empty cans up to a hundred feet away.

species.name: Greninja
species.desc: The Ninja Pokémon. It creates throwing stars out of compressed water. When it spins them and throws them at high speed, these stars can split metal in two.

species.name: Bunnelby
species.desc: The Digging Pokémon. They use their large ears to dig burrows. They will dig the whole night through.

species.name: Diggersby
species.desc: The Digging Pokémon. With their powerful ears, they can heft boulders of a ton or more with ease. They can be a big help at construction sites.

species.name: Fletchling
species.desc: The Tiny Robin Pokémon. These friendly Pokémon send signals to one another with beautiful chirps and tail-feather movements.

species.name: Fletchinder
species.desc: The Ember Pokémon. From its beak, it expels embers that set the tall grass on fire. Then it pounces on the bewildered prey that pop out of the grass.

species.name: Talonflame
species.desc: The Scorching Pokémon. In the fever of an exciting battle, it showers embers from the gaps between its feathers and takes to the air.

species.name: Scatterbug
species.desc: The Scatterdust Pokémon. When under attack from bird Pokémon, it spews a poisonous black powder that causes paralysis on contact.

species.name: Spewpa
species.desc: The Scatterdust Pokémon. It lives hidden within thicket shadows. When predators attack, it quickly bristles the fur covering its body in an effort to threaten them.

species.name: Vivillon
species.desc: The Scale Pokémon. Vivillon with many different patterns are found all over the world. These patterns are affected by the climate of their habitat.

species.name: Litleo
species.desc: The Lion Cub Pokémon. The stronger the opponent it faces, the more heat surges from its mane and the more power flows through its body.

species.name: Pyroar
species.desc: The Royal Pokémon. The male with the largest mane of fire is the leader of the pride.

species.name: Flabébé
species.desc: The Single Bloom Pokémon. It draws out and controls the hidden power of flowers. The flower Flabébé holds is most likely part of its body.

species.name: Floette
species.desc: The Single Bloom Pokémon. It flutters around fields of flowers and cares for flowers that are starting to wilt. It draws out the hidden power of flowers to battle.

species.name: Floette (Eternal Flower)
species.desc: The Single Bloom Pokémon. Terrifying energy is concealed within its ominous flower, but Floette still swings it about innocently.

species.name: Florges
species.desc: The Garden Pokémon. It claims exquisite flower gardens as its territory, and it obtains power from basking in the energy emitted by flowering plants.

species.name: Skiddo
species.desc: The Mount Pokémon. Thought to be one of the first Pokémon to live in harmony with humans, it has a placid disposition.

species.name: Gogoat
species.desc: The Mount Pokémon. It can tell how its Trainer is feeling by subtle shifts in the grip on its horns. This empathic sense lets them run as if one being.

species.name: Pancham
species.desc: The Playful Pokémon. It does its best to be taken seriously by its enemies, but its glare is not sufficiently intimidating. Chewing on a leaf is its trademark.
evTo: Pangoro (level 9, its trainer has another dark-type Pokemon in their party)

species.name: Pangoro
species.desc: The Daunting Pokémon. Although it possesses a violent temperament, it won't put up with bullying. It uses the leaf in its mouth to sense the movements of its enemies.

species.name: Furfrou
species.desc: The Poodle Pokémon. Trimming its fluffy fur not only makes it more elegant but also increases the swiftness of its movements.

species.name: Espurr
species.desc: The Restraint Pokémon. The organ that emits its intense psychic power is sheltered by its ears to keep power from leaking out.

species.name: Meowstic ♀
species.desc: The Constraint Pokémon. When in danger, it raises its ears and releases enough psychic power to grind a 10-ton truck into dust.

species.name: Meowstic ♂
species.desc: The Constraint Pokémon. When in danger, it raises its ears and releases enough psychic power to grind a 10-ton truck into dust.

species.name: Honedge
species.desc: The Sword Pokémon. Apparently this Pokémon is born when a departed spirit inhabits a sword. It attaches itself to people and drinks their life force.

species.name: Doublade
species.desc: The Sword Pokémon. When Honedge evolves, it divides into two swords, which cooperate via telepathy to coordinate attacks and slash their enemies to ribbons.

species.name: Aegislash
species.desc: The Royal Sword Pokémon. Generations of kings were attended by these Pokémon, which used their spectral power to manipulate and control people and Pokémon.

species.name: Spritzee
species.desc: The Perfume Pokémon. It emits a scent that enraptures those who smell it. This fragrance changes depending on what it has eaten.

species.name: Aromatisse
species.desc: The Fragrance Pokémon. It devises various scents, pleasant and unpleasant, and emits scents that its enemies dislike in order to gain an edge in battle.

species.name: Swirlix
species.desc: The Cotton Candy Pokémon. To entangle its opponents in battle, it extrudes white threads as sweet and sticky as cotton candy.

species.name: Slurpuff
species.desc: The Meringue Pokémon. It can distinguish the faintest of scents. It puts its sensitive sense of smell to use by helping pastry chefs in their work.

species.name: Inkay
species.desc: The Revolving Pokémon. Opponents who stare at the flashing of the light-emitting spots on its body become dazed and lose their will to fight.

species.name: Malamar
species.desc: The Overturning Pokémon. It wields the most compelling hypnotic powers of any Pokémon, and it forces others to do whatever it wants.

species.name: Binacle
species.desc: The Two-Handed Pokémon. Two Binacle live together on one rock. When they fight, one of them will move to a different rock.

species.name: Barbaracle
species.desc: The Collective Pokémon. When they evolve, two Binacle multiply into seven. They fight with the power of seven Binacle.

species.name: Skrelp
species.desc: The Mock Kelp Pokémon. Camouflaged as rotten kelp, they spray liquid poison on prey that approaches unawares and then finish it off.

species.name: Dragalge
species.desc: The Mock Kelp Pokémon. Their poison is strong enough to eat through the hull of a tanker, and they spit it indiscriminately at anything that enters their territory.

species.name: Clauncher
species.desc: The Water Gun Pokémon. They knock down flying prey by firing compressed water from their massive claws like shooting a pistol.

species.name: Clawitzer
species.desc: The Howitzer Pokémon. Their enormous claws launch cannonballs of water powerful enough to pierce tanker hulls.

species.name: Helioptile
species.desc: The Generator Pokémon. They make their home in deserts. They can generate their energy from basking in the sun, so eating food is not a requirement.

species.name: Heliolisk
species.desc: The Generator Pokémon. They flare their frills and generate energy. A single Heliolisk can generate sufficient electricity to power a skyscraper.

species.name: Tyrunt
species.desc: The Royal Heir Pokémon. This Pokémon was restored from a fossil. If something happens that it doesn't like, it throws a tantrum and runs wild.

species.name: Tyrantrum
species.desc: The Despot Pokémon. Thanks to its gargantuan jaws, which could shred thick metal plates as if they were paper, it was invincible in the ancient world it once inhabited.

species.name: Amaura
species.desc: The Tundra Pokémon. This ancient Pokémon was restored from part of its body that had been frozen in ice for over 100 million years.

species.name: Aurorus
species.desc: The Tundra Pokémon. The diamond-shaped crystals on its body expel air as cold as -240 degrees Fahrenheit, surrounding its enemies and encasing them in ice.

species.name: Sylveon
species.desc: The Intertwining Pokémon. It sends a soothing aura from its ribbonlike feelers to calm fights.

species.name: Hawlucha
species.desc: The Wrestling Pokémon. Although its body is small, its proficient fighting skills enable it to keep up with big bruisers like Machamp and Hariyama.

species.name: Dedenne
species.desc: The Antenna Pokémon. Its whiskers serve as antennas. By sending and receiving electrical waves, it can communicate with others over vast distances.

species.name: Carbink
species.desc: The Jewel Pokémon. Born from the temperatures and pressures deep underground, it fires beams from the stone in its head.

species.name: Goomy
species.desc: The Soft Tissue Pokémon. The weakest Dragon-type Pokémon, it lives in damp, shady places, so its body doesn't dry out.

species.name: Hisuian Sliggoo
species.desc: The Snail Pokémon. A creature given to melancholy. I suspect its metallic shell developed as a result of the mucus on its skin reacting with the iron in Hisui’s water.

species.name: Sliggoo
species.desc: The Soft Tissue Pokémon. It drives away opponents by excreting a sticky liquid that can dissolve anything. Its eyes devolved, so it can't see anything.

species.name: Goodra
species.desc: The Dragon Pokémon. This very friendly Dragon-type Pokémon will hug its beloved Trainer, leaving that Trainer covered in sticky slime.

species.name: Hisuian Goodra
species.desc: The Shell Bunker Pokémon. Able to freely control the hardness of its metallic shell. It loathes solitude and is extremely clingy—it will fume and run riot if those dearest to it ever leave its side.

species.name: Klefki
species.desc: The Key Ring Pokémon. These key collectors threaten any attackers by fiercely jingling their keys at them.

species.name: Phantump
species.desc: The Stump Pokémon. These Pokémon are created when spirits possess rotten tree stumps. They prefer to live in abandoned forests.

species.name: Trevenant
species.desc: The Elder Tree Pokémon. It can control trees at will. It will trap people who harm the forest, so they can never leave.

species.name: Pumpkaboo
species.desc: The Pumpkin Pokémon. The pumpkin body is inhabited by a spirit trapped in this world. As the sun sets, it becomes restless and active.

species.name: Gourgeist
species.desc: The Pumpkin Pokémon. Singing in eerie voices, they wander town streets on the night of the new moon. Anyone who hears their song is cursed.

species.name: Bergmite
species.desc: The Ice Chunk Pokémon. It blocks opponents' attacks with the ice that shields its body. It uses cold air to repair any cracks with new ice.

species.name: Avalugg
species.desc: The Iceberg Pokémon. Its ice-covered body is as hard as steel. Its cumbersome frame crushes anything that stands in its way.

species.name: Hisuian Avalugg
species.desc: The Iceberg Pokémon. The armor of ice covering its lower jaw puts steel to shame and can shatter rocks with ease. This Pokémon barrels along steep mountain paths, cleaving through the deep snow.

species.name: Noibat
species.desc: The Sound Wave Pokémon. They live in pitch-black caves. Their enormous ears can emit ultrasonic waves of 200,000 hertz.

species.name: Noivern
species.desc: The Sound Wave Pokémon. They fly around on moonless nights and attack careless prey. Nothing can beat them in a battle in the dark.

species.name: Xerneas
species.desc: The Life Pokémon. Legends say it can share eternal life. It slept for a thousand years in the form of a tree before its revival.

species.name: Yveltal
species.desc: The Destruction Pokémon. When this legendary Pokémon's wings and tail feathers spread wide and glow red, it absorbs the life force of living creatures.

species.name: Zygarde 10% Forme
species.desc: The Order Pokémon. Its sharp fangs make short work of finishing off its enemies, but it's unable to maintain this body indefinitely. After a period of time, it falls apart.

species.name: Zygarde 50% Forme
species.desc: The Order Pokémon. This is Zygarde's form when it has gathered 50% of its cells. It wipes out all those who oppose it, showing not a shred of mercy.

species.name: Zygarde Complete Forme
species.desc: The Order Pokémon. This is Zygarde's form at times when it uses its overwhelming power to suppress those who endanger the ecosystem.

species.name: Diancie
species.desc: The Jewel Pokémon. A sudden transformation of Carbink, its pink, glimmering body is said to be the loveliest sight in the whole world.

species.name: Hoopa Confined
species.desc: The Mischief Pokémon. In its true form, it possesses a huge amount of power. Legends of its avarice tell how it once carried off an entire castle to gain the treasure hidden within.

species.name: Hoopa Unbound
species.desc: The Mischief Pokémon. In its true form, it possesses a huge amount of power. Legends of its avarice tell how it once carried off an entire castle to gain the treasure hidden within.

species.name: Volcanion
species.desc: The Steam Pokémon. It lets out billows of steam and disappears into the dense fog. It's said to live in mountains where humans do not tread.

species.name: Rowlet
species.desc: The Grass Quill Pokémon. It sends its feathers, which are as sharp as blades, flying in attack. Its legs are strong, so its kicks are also formidable.

species.name: Dartrix
species.desc: The Blade Quill Pokémon. This narcissistic Pokémon is a clean freak. If you don’t groom it diligently, it will stop listening to you.

species.name: Decidueye
species.desc: The Arrow Quill Pokémon. It nocks its arrow quills and shoots them at opponents. When it simply can’t afford to miss, it tugs the vine on its head to improve its focus.

species.name: Hisuian Decidueye
species.desc: The Arrow Quill Pokémon. The air stored inside the rachises of Decidueye’s feathers insulates the Pokémon against Hisui’s extreme cold. This is firm proof that evolution can be influenced by environment.

species.name: Litten
species.desc: The Fire Cat Pokémon. If you try too hard to get close to it, it won’t open up to you. Even if you do grow close, giving it too much affection is still a no-no.

species.name: Torracat
species.desc: The Fire Cat Pokémon. It can act spoiled if it grows close to its Trainer. A powerful Pokémon, its sharp claws can leave its Trainer’s whole body covered in scratches.

species.name: Incineroar
species.desc: The Heel Pokémon. Although it’s rough mannered and egotistical, it finds beating down unworthy opponents boring. It gets motivated for stronger opponents.

species.name: Popplio
species.desc: The Sea Lion Pokémon. The balloons it inflates with its nose grow larger and larger as it practices day by day.

species.name: Brionne
species.desc: The Pop Star Pokémon. It gets excited when it sees a dance it doesn’t know. This hard worker practices diligently until it can learn that dance.

species.name: Primarina
species.desc: The Soloist Pokémon. To Primarina, every battle is a stage. It takes down its prey with beautiful singing and dancing.

species.name: Pikipek
species.desc: The Woodpecker Pokémon. It pecks at trees with its hard beak. You can get some idea of its mood or condition from the rhythm of its pecking.

species.name: Trumbeak
species.desc: The Bugle Beak Pokémon. It can bend the tip of its beak to produce over a hundred different cries at will.

species.name: Toucannon
species.desc: The Cannon Pokémon. They smack beaks with others of their kind to communicate. The strength and number of hits tell each other how they feel.

species.name: Yungoos
species.desc: The Loitering Pokémon. Its stomach takes up most of its long torso. It’s a big eater, so the amount Trainers have to spend on its food is no laughing matter.

species.name: Gumshoos
species.desc: The Stakeout Pokémon. Although it wasn’t originally found in Alola, this Pokémon was brought over a long time ago when there was a huge Rattata outbreak.

species.name: Grubbin
species.desc: The Larva Pokémon. If you find its nest, you shouldn’t stick your hand inside. You’ll get bitten by an irritated Grubbin.

species.name: Charjabug
species.desc: The Battery Pokémon. It buries itself in fallen leaves and barely moves, munching away on humus. If you accidentally step on one, you’ll get a shock!

species.name: Vikavolt
species.desc: The Stag Beetle Pokémon. It has an organ that generates electricity in its abdomen. It concentrates energy in its strong jaws and fires off powerful jolts of electricity.

species.name: Crabrawler
species.desc: The Boxing Pokémon. Its hard pincers are well suited to both offense and defense. Fights between two Crabrawler are like boxing matches.

species.name: Crabominable
species.desc: The Woolly Crab Pokémon. It stores coldness in its pincers and pummels its foes. It can even smash thick walls of ice to bits!

species.name: Oricorio Baile Style
species.desc: The Dancing Pokémon. It wins the hearts of its enemies with its passionate dancing and then uses the opening it creates to burn them up with blazing flames.

species.name: Oricorio Pa'u Style
species.desc: The Dancing Pokémon. It relaxes its opponents with its elegant dancing. When they let their guard down, it showers them with psychic energy.

species.name: Oricorio Pom-Pom Style
species.desc: The Dancing Pokémon. It lifts its opponents’ spirits with its cheerful dance moves. When they let their guard down, it electrocutes them with a jolt.

species.name: Oricorio Sensu Style
species.desc: The Dancing Pokémon. It charms its opponents with its refined dancing. When they let their guard down, it places a curse on them that will bring on their demise.

species.name: Cutiefly
species.desc: The Bee Fly Pokémon. Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. In fields of flowers, it gets into skirmishes with Butterfree over food.

species.name: Ribombee
species.desc: The Bee Fly Pokémon. Rain makes pollen damp, so Ribombee hates rain. When it sees ominous clouds, it finds a hollow in a tree, where it waits stock-still.

species.name: Rockruff
species.desc: The Puppy Pokémon. As they develop, their disposition grows more violent and aggressive. Many Trainers find them too much to handle and abandon them.
evTo: Lycanroc Midday Form (level 9, during the morning)
Lycanroc Midnight Form (level 9, during the night)
Lycanroc Dusk Form (level 9, during the afternoon)

species.name: Lycanroc Dusk Form
species.desc: The Wolf Pokémon. Bathed in the setting sun of evening, Lycanroc has undergone a special kind of evolution. An intense fighting spirit underlies its calmness.

species.name: Lycanroc Midday Form
species.desc: The Wolf Pokémon. The sharp rocks in its mane can cut like knives. Lycanroc wears its prey down by degrees before finishing them off.

species.name: Lycanroc Midnight Form
species.desc: The Wolf Pokémon. It has no problem ignoring orders it doesn’t like. It doesn’t seem to mind getting hurt at all—as long as it can finish off its opponent.

species.name: Wishiwashi School Form
species.desc: The Small Fry Pokémon. Wishiwashi assemble in this formation to face off against strong foes. It boasts a strength that earned it the name “demon of the sea.”

species.name: Wishiwashi Solo Form
species.desc: The Small Fry Pokémon. They’re weak, so they move in schools. However, they can also often be seen all alone, having strayed from the school.

species.name: Mareanie
species.desc: The Brutal Star Pokémon. They eat Corsola branches, so Mareanie are hated by craftsmen who work with Corsola branches that have naturally fallen off.

species.name: Toxapex
species.desc: The Brutal Star Pokémon. To attack, this Pokémon sends toxic spikes flying at its enemies. Ones that come close get mown down by the claws on its feet.

species.name: Mudbray
species.desc: The Donkey Pokémon. It loves playing in the mud. If it isn’t showered with mud on a daily basis, it gets stressed out and stops listening to its Trainer.

species.name: Mudsdale
species.desc: The Draft Horse Pokémon. It remains calm and unmoving no matter the situation. It mixes dirt with the saliva in its mouth to make a special kind of mud.

species.name: Dewpider
species.desc: The Water Bubble Pokémon. When two Dewpider meet, they display their water bubbles to each other. Then the one with the smaller bubble gets out of the other’s way.

species.name: Araquanid
species.desc: The Water Bubble Pokémon. It usually passes its time in the water. When its belly is full, it stores its subdued prey in the water bubble on its head.

species.name: Fomantis
species.desc: The Sickle Grass Pokémon. When the sun rises, Fomantis spreads its four leaves and bathes in the sunlight. The tip of its head has a pleasant aroma.

species.name: Lurantis
species.desc: The Bloom Sickle Pokémon. For self-protection, it pretends to be a bug Pokémon. Both of its arms bear keen-edged petals.

species.name: Morelull
species.desc: The Illuminating Pokémon. It scatters its shining spores around itself. Even though they’re dangerous, nighttime tours of forests where Morelull live are popular.

species.name: Shiinotic
species.desc: The Illuminating Pokémon. It puts its prey to sleep and siphons off their vitality through the tip of its arms. If one of its kind is weakened, it helps by sending it vitality.

species.name: Salandit
species.desc: The Toxic Lizard Pokémon. The males will do whatever the females tell them. They give the females most of their food. Due to malnutrition, the males can’t evolve.

species.name: Salazzle
species.desc: The Toxic Lizard Pokémon. Salazzle lives deep in caves and forces the Salandit it has attracted with its pheromones to serve it.

species.name: Stufful
species.desc: The Flailing Pokémon. It boasts power enough to split large trees in half. The organ on its rear releases an odor that it uses to communicate with others of its kind.

species.name: Bewear
species.desc: The Strong Arm Pokémon. It waves its hands wildly in intimidation and warning. Life is over for anyone who doesn’t run away as fast as possible.

species.name: Bounsweet
species.desc: The Fruit Pokémon. Because of its sweet, delicious aroma, bird Pokémon are always after it, but it’s not intelligent enough to care.

species.name: Steenee
species.desc: The Fruit Pokémon. It’s protected by its hard sepals, so it plays with bird Pokémon without worry. They peck it relentlessly, but it doesn’t care.

species.name: Tsareena
species.desc: The Fruit Pokémon. A master of grand and beautiful kicks, it can knock out even kickboxing champions with a single blow.

species.name: Comfey
species.desc: The Posy Picker Pokémon. It stretches sticky vines out from its head and picks flowers to adorn itself with. When it doesn’t have any flowers, it feels uneasy.

species.name: Oranguru
species.desc: The Sage Pokémon. It normally spends its time meditating in the treetops. It throws Poké Balls and gives other Pokémon orders as it pleases.

species.name: Passimian
species.desc: The Teamwork Pokémon. They use their saliva to stick leaves to their shoulders. You can tell what troop they belong to from the position of the leaves.

species.name: Wimpod
species.desc: The Turn Tail Pokémon. It will pick up anything it finds on the ground. Sometimes it finds coins, so Murkrow and Meowth will go after it.

species.name: Golisopod
species.desc: The Hard Scale Pokémon. The shell covering its body is as hard as diamond. This Pokémon will do anything it takes to win.

species.name: Sandygast
species.desc: The Sand Heap Pokémon. It likes the shovel on its head, so Sandygast will get serious and fight any children who come to take it back.

species.name: Palossand
species.desc: The Sand Castle Pokémon. Each of its grains of sand has its own will. Palossand eats small Pokémon and siphons away their vital essence while they’re still alive.

species.name: Pyukumuku
species.desc: The Sea Cucumber Pokémon. The tradition known as Pyukumuku chucking started from the custom of throwing Pyukumuku back into the sea after they wash onshore.

species.name: Type: Null
species.desc: The Synthetic Pokémon. A Pokémon weapon developed for a specific mission, it went berserk during an experiment, so it was cryogenically frozen.

species.name: Silvally
species.desc: The Synthetic Pokémon. This is its form once it has awakened and evolved. Freed from its heavy mask, its speed is greatly increased.

species.name: Minior Core Form
species.desc: The Meteor Pokémon. Places where Minior fall from the night sky are few and far between, with Alola being one of the precious few.

species.name: Minior Meteor Form
species.desc: The Meteor Pokémon. It lives in the ozone layer, where it becomes food for stronger Pokémon. When it tries to run away, it falls to the ground.

species.name: Komala
species.desc: The Drowsing Pokémon. It stays asleep from the moment it’s born. When it falls into a deep sleep, it stops moving altogether.

species.name: Turtonator
species.desc: The Blast Turtle Pokémon. It lives in volcanoes and eats sulfur and other minerals. Materials from the food it eats form the basis of its explosive shell.

species.name: Togedemaru
species.desc: The Roly-Poly Pokémon. When it’s surprised or agitated, the 14 fur spikes on its back will stand up involuntarily.

species.name: Mimikyu
species.desc: The Disguise Pokémon. It stands in front of a mirror, trying to fix its broken neck as if its life depended on it. It has a hard time getting it right, so it’s crying inside.

species.name: Bruxish
species.desc: The Gnash Teeth Pokémon. It burrows beneath the sand, radiating psychic power from the protuberance on its head. It waits for prey as it surveys the area.

species.name: Drampa
species.desc: The Placid Pokémon. If a child it has made friends with is bullied, Drampa will find the bully’s house and burn it to the ground.

species.name: Dhelmise
species.desc: The Sea Creeper Pokémon. It wraps its prey in green seaweed and sucks away their vitality. It only likes to go after big prey like Wailord.

species.name: Jangmo-o
species.desc: The Scaly Pokémon. It smacks the scales on its head against rocks or against the ground to frighten its opponents. It can also contact its friends with these noises.

species.name: Hakamo-o
species.desc: The Scaly Pokémon. It makes noise by clanging its scales together. When the rhythm has reached its peak, Hakamo-o attacks.

species.name: Kommo-o
species.desc: The Scaly Pokémon. When it howls after finishing off its prey, the metallic sounds of its celebrating comrades can be heard from all around.

species.name: Tapu Koko
species.desc: The Land Spirit Pokémon. Although it’s called a guardian deity, if a person or Pokémon puts it in a bad mood, it will become a malevolent deity and attack.

species.name: Tapu Lele
species.desc: The Land Spirit Pokémon. As it flutters about, it scatters its strangely glowing scales. Touching them is said to restore good health on the spot.

species.name: Tapu Bulu
species.desc: The Land Spirit Pokémon. Although it’s called a guardian deity, it’s violent enough to crush anyone it sees as an enemy.

species.name: Tapu Fini
species.desc: The Land Spirit Pokémon. This guardian deity of Poni Island manipulates water. Because it lives deep within a thick fog, it came to be both feared and revered.

species.name: Cosmog
species.desc: The Nebula Pokémon. Even though its helpless, gaseous body can be blown away by the slightest breeze, it doesn’t seem to care.

species.name: Cosmoem
species.desc: The Protostar Pokémon. The king who ruled Alola in times of antiquity called it the “cocoon of the stars” and built an altar to worship it.

species.name: Solgaleo
species.desc: The Sunne Pokémon. Sometimes the result of its opening an Ultra Wormhole is that energy and life-forms from other worlds are called here to this world.

species.name: Lunala
species.desc: The Moone Pokémon. Records of it exist in writings from long, long ago, where it was known by the name “the beast that calls the moon.”

species.name: Nihilego
species.desc: The Parasite Pokémon. A life-form from another world, it was dubbed an Ultra Beast and is thought to produce a strong neurotoxin.

species.name: Buzzwole
species.desc: The Swollen Pokémon. Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

species.name: Pheromosa
species.desc: The Lissome Pokémon. A life-form that lives in another world, its body is thin and supple, but it also possesses great power.

species.name: Xurkitree
species.desc: The Glowing Pokémon. Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

species.name: Celesteela
species.desc: The Launch Pokémon. One kind of Ultra Beast. Witnesses have seen it burn down a forest by expelling gas from its two arms.

species.name: Kartana
species.desc: The Drawn Sword Pokémon. This Ultra Beast’s body, which is as thin as paper, is like a sharpened sword.

species.name: Guzzlord
species.desc: The Junkivore Pokémon. Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

species.name: Dawn Wings Necrozma
species.desc: The Prism Pokémon. This is its form while it’s devouring the light of Lunala. It grasps foes in its giant claws and rips them apart with brute force.

species.name: Dusk Mane Necrozma
species.desc: The Prism Pokémon. This is Necrozma’s form while it’s absorbing the power of Solgaleo, making it extremely ferocious and impossible to control.

species.name: Necrozma
species.desc: The Prism Pokémon. It looks somehow pained as it rages around in search of light, which serves as its energy. It’s apparently from another world.

species.name: Ultra Necrozma
species.desc: The Prism Pokémon. The light pouring out from all over its body affects living things and nature, impacting them in various ways.

species.name: Magearna
species.desc: The Artificial Pokémon. It synchronizes its consciousness with others to understand their feelings. This faculty makes it useful for taking care of people.

species.name: Marshadow
species.desc: The Gloomdweller Pokémon. It slips into the shadows of others and mimics their powers and movements. As it improves, it becomes stronger than those it’s imitating.

species.name: Poipole
species.desc: The Poison Pin Pokémon. An Ultra Beast that lives in a different world, it cackles wildly as it sprays its opponents with poison from the needles on its head.

species.name: Naganadel
species.desc: The Poison Pin Pokémon. One kind of Ultra Beast, it fires a glowing, venomous liquid from its needles. This liquid is also immensely adhesive.

species.name: Stakataka
species.desc: The Rampart Pokémon. It appeared from an Ultra Wormhole. Each one appears to be made up of many life-forms stacked one on top of each other.

species.name: Blacephalon
species.desc: The Fireworks Pokémon. It slithers toward people. Then, without warning, it triggers the explosion of its own head. It’s apparently one kind of Ultra Beast.

species.name: Zeraora
species.desc: The Thunderclap Pokémon. It electrifies its claws and tears its opponents apart with them. Even if they dodge its attack, they’ll be electrocuted by the flying sparks.

species.name: Meltan
species.desc: The Hex Nut Pokémon. It dissolves and eats metal. Circulating liquid metal within its body is how it generates energy.

species.name: Melmetal
species.desc: The Hex Nut Pokémon. At the end of its life-span, Melmetal will rust and fall apart. The small shards left behind will eventually be reborn as Meltan.

species.name: Grookey
species.desc: The Chimp Pokémon. Grookey attacks by beating with a stick. As the speed of its beats increases, Grookey's excitement does too.

species.name: Thwackey
species.desc: The Beat Pokémon. The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.

species.name: Rillaboom
species.desc: The Drummer Pokémon. By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.

species.name: Scorbunny
species.desc: The Rabbit Pokémon. A warm-up of running around gets fire energy coursing through this Pokémon's body. Once that happens, it's ready to fight at full power.

species.name: Raboot
species.desc: The Rabbit Pokémon. It kicks berries right off the branches of trees and then juggles them with its feet, practicing its footwork.

species.name: Cinderace
species.desc: The Striker Pokémon. It juggles a pebble with its feet, turning it into a burning soccer ball. Its shots strike opponents hard and leave them scorched.

species.name: Sobble
species.desc: The Water Lizard Pokémon. When scared, this Pokémon cries. Its tears pack the chemical punch of 100 onions, and attackers won't be able to resist weeping.

species.name: Drizzile
species.desc: The Water Lizard Pokémon. A clever combatant, this Pokémon battles using water balloons created with moisture secreted from its palms.

species.name: Inteleon
species.desc: The Secret Agent Pokémon. It has many hidden capabilities, such as fingertips that can shoot water and a membrane on its back that it can use to glide through the air.

species.name: Skwovet
species.desc: The Cheeky Pokémon. It eats berries nonstop—a habit that has made it more resilient than it looks. It'll show up on farms, searching for yet more berries.

species.name: Greedent
species.desc: The Greedy Pokémon. It stashes berries in its tail—so many berries that they fall out constantly. But this Pokémon is a bit slow-witted, so it doesn't notice the loss.

species.name: Rookidee
species.desc: The Tiny Bird Pokémon. Jumping nimbly about, this small-bodied Pokémon takes advantage of even the slightest opportunity to disorient larger opponents.

species.name: Corvisquire
species.desc: The Raven Pokémon. Smart enough to use tools in battle, these Pokémon have been seen picking up rocks and flinging them or using ropes to wrap up enemies.

species.name: Corviknight
species.desc: The Raven Pokémon. With their great intellect and flying skills, the black luster of its steel body could drive terror into the heart of any foe.

species.name: Blipbug
species.desc: The Larva Pokémon. Often found in gardens, this Pokémon has hairs on its body that it uses to assess its surroundings.

species.name: Dottler
species.desc: The Radome Pokémon. It barely moves, but it's still alive. Hiding in its shell without food or water seems to have awakened its psychic powers.

species.name: Orbeetle
species.desc: The Seven Spot Pokémon. It's famous for its high level of intelligence, and the large size of its brain is proof that it also possesses immense psychic power.

species.name: Nickit
species.desc: The Fox Pokémon. Cunning and cautious, this Pokémon survives by stealing food from others. It erases its tracks with swipes of its tail as it makes off with its plunder.

species.name: Thievul
species.desc: The Fox Pokémon. It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it.

species.name: Gossifleur
species.desc: The Flowering Pokémon. It anchors itself in the ground with its single leg, then basks in the sun. After absorbing enough sunlight, its petals spread as it blooms brilliantly.

species.name: Eldegoss
species.desc: The Cotton Bloom Pokémon. The seeds attached to its cotton fluff are full of nutrients. It spreads them on the wind so that plants and other Pokémon can benefit from them.

species.name: Wooloo
species.desc: The Sheep Pokémon. Its curly fleece is such an effective cushion that this Pokémon could fall off a cliff and stand right back up at the bottom, unharmed.

species.name: Dubwool
species.desc: The Sheep Pokémon. Weave a carpet from its springy wool, and you end up with something closer to a trampoline. You'll start to bounce the moment you set foot on it.

species.name: Chewtle
species.desc: The Snapping Pokémon. It starts off battles by attacking with its rock-hard horn, but as soon as the opponent flinches, this Pokémon bites down and never lets go.

species.name: Drednaw
species.desc: The Bite Pokémon. With jaws that can shear through steel rods, this highly aggressive Pokémon chomps down on its unfortunate prey.

species.name: Yamper
species.desc: The Puppy Pokémon. This gluttonous Pokémon only assists people with their work because it wants treats. As it runs, it crackles with electricity.

species.name: Boltund
species.desc: The Dog Pokémon. This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.

species.name: Rolycoly
species.desc: The Coal Pokémon. Most of its body has the same composition as coal. Fittingly, this Pokémon was first discovered in coal mines about 400 years ago.

species.name: Carkol
species.desc: The Coal Pokémon. By rapidly rolling its legs, it can travel at over 18 mph. The temperature of the flames it breathes exceeds 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit.

species.name: Coalossal
species.desc: The Coal Pokémon. While it's engaged in battle, its mountain of coal will burn bright red, sending off sparks that scorch the surrounding area.

species.name: Applin
species.desc: The Apple Core Pokémon. It spends its entire life inside an apple. It hides from its natural enemies, bird Pokémon, by pretending it's just an apple and nothing more.
evTo: Flapple (level 5, inhabiting a green or gold apple)

species.name: Flapple
species.desc: The Apple Wing Pokémon. It flies on wings of apple skin and spits a powerful acid. It can also change its shape into that of an apple.

species.name: Appletun
species.desc: The Apple Nectar Pokémon. Its body is covered in sweet nectar, and the skin on its back is especially yummy. A nectarous scent wafts from its body, luring in the bug Pokémon it preys on.

species.name: Silicobra
species.desc: The Sand Snake Pokémon. As it digs, it swallows sand and stores it in its neck pouch. The pouch can hold more than 17 pounds of sand.

species.name: Sandaconda
species.desc: The Sand Snake Pokémon. When it contracts its body, over 220 pounds of sand sprays from its nose. If it ever runs out of sand, it becomes disheartened.

species.name: Cramorant
species.desc: The Gulp Pokémon. This hungry Pokémon swallows Arrokuda whole. Occasionally, it makes a mistake and tries to swallow a Pokémon other than its preferred prey.

species.name: Arrokuda
species.desc: The Rush Pokémon. If it sees any movement around it, this Pokémon charges for it straightaway, leading with its sharply pointed jaw. It's very proud of that jaw.

species.name: Barraskewda
species.desc: The Skewer Pokémon. It spins its tail fins to propel itself, surging forward at speeds of over 100 knots before ramming prey and spearing into them.

species.name: Toxel
species.desc: The Baby Pokémon. It stores poison in an internal poison sac and secretes that poison through its skin. If you touch this Pokémon, a tingling sensation follows.
evTo: Toxtricity (Amped) (level 8, its nature is Hardy, Brave, Adamant, Naughty, Docile, Impish, Lax, Hasty, Jolly, Naive, Rash, Sassy, or Quirky)
Toxtricity (Low Key) (level 8, its nature is NOT Hardy, Brave, Adamant, Naughty, Docile, Impish, Lax, Hasty, Jolly, Naive, Rash, Sassy, or Quirky)

species.name: Toxtricity (Amped)
species.desc: The Punk Pokémon. This short-tempered and aggressive Pokémon chugs stagnant water to absorb any toxins it might contain.

species.name: Toxtricity (Low Key)
species.desc: The Punk Pokémon. Capable of generating 15,000 volts of electricity, this Pokémon looks down on all that would challenge it.

species.name: Sizzlipede
species.desc: The Radiator Pokémon. It wraps prey up with its heated body, cooking them in its coils. Once they're well-done, it will voraciously nibble them down to the last morsel.

species.name: Centiskorch
species.desc: The Radiator Pokémon. When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.

species.name: Clobbopus
species.desc: The Tantrum Pokémon. It's very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land.

species.name: Grapploct
species.desc: The Tantrum Pokémon. A body made up of nothing but muscle makes the grappling moves this Pokémon performs with its tentacles tremendously powerful.

species.name: Sinistea
species.desc: The Black Tea Pokémon. This Pokémon is said to have been born when a lonely spirit possessed a cold, leftover cup of tea.

species.name: Polteageist
species.desc: The Black Tea Pokémon. This species lives in antique teapots. Most pots are forgeries, but on rare occasions, an authentic work is found.

species.name: Hatenna
species.desc: The Calm Pokémon. Via the protrusion on its head, it senses other creatures’ emotions. If you don’t have a calm disposition, it will never warm up to you.

species.name: Hattrem
species.desc: The Serene Pokémon. No matter who you are, if you bring strong emotions near this Pokémon, it will silence you violently.

species.name: Hatterene
species.desc: The Silent Pokémon. It emits psychic power strong enough to cause headaches as a deterrent to the approach of others.

species.name: Impidimp
species.desc: The Wily Pokémon. Through its nose, it sucks in the emanations produced by people and Pokémon when they feel annoyed. It thrives off this negative energy.

species.name: Morgrem
species.desc: The Devious Pokémon. When it gets down on all fours as if to beg for forgiveness, it’s trying to lure opponents in so that it can stab them with its spear-like hair.

species.name: Grimmsnarl
species.desc: The Bulk Up Pokémon. With the hair wrapped around its body helping to enhance its muscles, this Pokémon can overwhelm even Machamp.

species.name: Obstagoon
species.desc: The Blocking Pokémon. It evolved after experiencing numerous fights. While crossing its arms, it lets out a shout that would make any opponent flinch.

species.name: Perrserker
species.desc: The Scratch Cat Pokémon. What appears to be an iron helmet is actually hardened hair. This Pokémon lives for the thrill of battle.

species.name: Cursola
species.desc: The Coral Pokémon. Its shell is overflowing with its heightened otherworldly energy. The ectoplasm serves as protection for this Pokémon's core spirit.

species.name: Sirfetch'd
species.desc: The Wild Duck Pokémon. Only Farfetch'd that have survived many battles can attain this evolution. When this Pokémon's leek withers, it will retire from combat.

species.name: Mr. Rime
species.desc: The Dancing Pokémon. It's highly skilled at tap-dancing. It waves its cane of ice in time with its graceful movements.

species.name: Runerigus
species.desc: The Grudge Pokémon. Never touch its shadowlike body, or you'll be shown the horrific memories behind the picture carved into it.

species.name: Milcery
species.desc: The Cream Pokémon. They say that any patisserie visited by Milcery is guaranteed success and good fortune.

species.name: Alcremie
species.desc: The Cream Pokémon. Alcremie can produce whipped cream, which becomes richer the happier Alcremie is feeling. Desserts made using this cream are invariably delicious, so many pastry chefs strive to have an Alcremie as their partner.

species.name: Falinks
species.desc: The Formation Pokémon. The leader, known as the brass, uses its extendible horn to issue orders to the others when it’s time to change formation.

species.name: Pincurchin
species.desc: The Sea Urchin Pokémon. This Pokémon is so timid that even brushing against seaweed will make it discharge electricity in surprise. Its lips do not conduct electricity.

species.name: Snom
species.desc: The Worm Pokemon. Within its internal organs, Snom amplifies the frigid air it gets from eating snow and then uses this amplified air to create icicle-like spikes.

species.name: Frosmoth
species.desc: The Frost Moth Pokémon. Icy scales fall from its wings like snow as it flies over fields and mountains. The temperature of its wings is less than -290 degrees Fahrenheit.

species.name: Stonjourner
species.desc: The Big Rock Pokémon. It stands in grasslands, watching the sun’s descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.

species.name: Eiscue
species.desc: The Penguin Pokémon. It drifted in on the flow of ocean waters from a frigid place. It keeps its head iced constantly to make sure it stays nice and cold.

species.name: Indeedee ♀
species.desc: The Emotion Pokémon. They diligently serve people and Pokémon so they can gather feelings of gratitude. The females are particularly good at babysitting.

species.name: Indeedee ♂
species.desc: The Emotion Pokémon. It uses the horns on its head to sense the emotions of others. Males will act as valets for those they serve, looking after their every need.

species.name: Morpeko
species.desc: The Two-Sided Pokémon. As it eats the seeds stored up in its pocket-like pouches, this Pokémon is not just satisfying its constant hunger. It’s also generating electricity.

species.name: Cufant
species.desc: The Copperderm Pokémon. It digs up the ground with its trunk. It’s also very strong, being able to carry loads of over five tons without any problem at all.

species.name: Copperajah
species.desc: The Copperderm Pokémon. They came over from another region long ago and worked together with humans. Their green skin is resistant to water.

species.name: Dracozolt
species.desc: The Fossil Pokémon. In ancient times, it was unbeatable thanks to its powerful lower body, but it went extinct anyway after it depleted all its plant-based food sources.

species.name: Arctozolt
species.desc: The Fossil Pokémon. The shaking of its freezing upper half is what generates its electricity. It has a hard time walking around.

species.name: Dracovish
species.desc: The Fossil Pokémon. Powerful legs and jaws made it the apex predator of its time. Its own overhunting of its prey was what drove it to extinction.

species.name: Arctovish
species.desc: The Fossil Pokémon. Though it’s able to capture prey by freezing its surroundings, it has trouble eating the prey afterward because its mouth is on top of its head.

species.name: Duraludon
species.desc: The Alloy Pokémon. Its body resembles polished metal, and it’s both lightweight and strong. The only drawback is that it rusts easily.

species.name: Dreepy
species.desc: The Lingering Pokémon. After being reborn as a ghost Pokémon, Dreepy wanders the areas it used to inhabit back when it was alive in prehistoric seas.

species.name: Drakloak
species.desc: The Caretaker Pokémon. It’s capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve.

species.name: Dragapult
species.desc: The Stealth Pokémon. When it isn’t battling, it keeps Dreepy in the holes on its horns. Once a fight starts, it launches the Dreepy like supersonic missiles.

species.name: Zacian
species.desc: The Warrior Pokémon. Known as a legendary hero, this Pokémon absorbs metal particles, transforming them into a weapon it uses to battle.

species.name: Zacian (Crowned)
species.desc: The Warrior Pokémon. Known as a legendary hero, this Pokémon absorbs metal particles, transforming them into a weapon it uses to battle.

species.name: Zamazenta
species.desc: The Warrior Pokémon. In times past, it worked together with a king of the people to save the Galar region. It absorbs metal that it then uses in battle.

species.name: Zamazenta (Crowned)
species.desc: The Warrior Pokémon. In times past, it worked together with a king of the people to save the Galar region. It absorbs metal that it then uses in battle.

species.name: Eternatus
species.desc: The Gigantic Pokémon. The core on its chest absorbs energy emanating from the lands of the Galar region. This energy is what allows Eternatus to stay active.

species.name: Eternatus (Eternamax)
species.desc: The Gigantic Pokémon. The core on its chest absorbs energy emanating from the lands of the Galar region. This energy is what allows Eternatus to stay active.

species.name: Kubfu
species.desc: The Wushu Pokémon. Kubfu trains hard to perfect its moves. The moves it masters will determine which form it takes when it evolves.
evTo: Urshifu (Single Strike) (level 10, using Scroll of Darkness)
Urshifu (Rapid Strike) (level 10, using Scroll of Waters)

species.name: Urshifu (Rapid Strike)
species.desc: The Wushu Pokémon. This form of Urshifu is a strong believer in defeating foes by raining many blows down on them. Its strikes are nonstop, flowing like a river.

species.name: Urshifu (Single Strike)
species.desc: The Wushu Pokémon. This form of Urshifu is a strong believer in the one-hit KO. Its strategy is to leap in close to foes and land a devastating blow with a hardened fist.

species.name: Zarude
species.desc: The Rogue Monkey Pokémon. Within dense forests, this Pokémon lives in a pack with others of its kind. It’s incredibly aggressive, and the other Pokémon of the forest fear it.

species.name: Regieleki
species.desc: The Electron Pokémon. This Pokémon is a cluster of electrical energy. It’s said that removing the rings on Regieleki’s body will unleash the Pokémon’s latent power.

species.name: Regidrago
species.desc: The Dragon Orb Pokémon. An academic theory proposes that Regidrago’s arms were once the head of an ancient dragon Pokémon. The theory remains unproven.

species.name: Glastrier
species.desc: The Wild Horse Pokémon. Glastrier emits intense cold from its hooves. It’s also a belligerent Pokémon—anything it wants, it takes by force.

species.name: Spectrier
species.desc: The Swift Horse Pokémon. It probes its surroundings with all its senses save one—it doesn’t use its sense of sight. Spectrier’s kicks are said to separate soul from body.

species.name: Calyrex
species.desc: The King Pokémon. Calyrex is a merciful Pokémon, capable of providing healing and blessings. It reigned over the Galar region in times of yore.

species.name: Calyrex (Ice Rider)
species.desc: The High King Pokémon. According to lore, this Pokémon showed no mercy to those who got in its way, yet it would heal its opponents’ wounds after battle.

species.name: Calyrex (Shadow Rider)
species.desc: The High King Pokémon. Legend says that by using its power to see all events from past to future, this Pokémon saved the creatures of a forest from a meteorite strike.

species.name: Wyrdeer
species.desc: The Big Horn Pokémon. The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.

species.name: Kleavor
species.desc: The Axe Pokémon. A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.

species.name: Bloodmoon Ursaluna
species.desc: The Peat Pokémon. This special Ursaluna can see in the dark with its left eye and protects itself with mud that is as hard as iron.

species.name: Ursaluna
species.desc: The Peat Pokémon. I believe it was Hisui's swampy terrain that gave Ursaluna its burly physique and newfound capacity to manipulate peat at will.

species.name: Basculegion ♀
species.desc: The Big Fish Pokémon. Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui's rivers is Basculegion's equal.

species.name: Basculegion ♂
species.desc: The Big Fish Pokémon. Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui's rivers is Basculegion's equal.

species.name: Sneasler
species.desc: The Free Climb Pokémon. Because of Sneasler's virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.

species.name: Overqwil
species.desc: The Pin Cluster Pokémon. Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname ”sea fiend.” It slurps up poison to nourish itself.

species.name: Enamorus (Incarnate)
species.desc: The Love-Hate Pokémon. When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon's love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.

species.name: Enamorus (Therian)
species.desc: The Love-Hate Pokémon. When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon's love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.

species.name: Sprigatito
species.desc: The Grass Cat Pokemon. The sweet scent its body gives off mesmerizes those around it. The scent grows stronger when this Pokémon is in the sun.

species.name: Floragato
species.desc: The Grass Cat Pokémon. The hardness of Floragato’s fur depends on the Pokémon’s mood. When Floragato is prepared to battle, its fur becomes pointed and needle sharp.

species.name: Meowscarada
species.desc: The Magician Pokémon. With skillful misdirection, it rigs foes with pollen-packed flower bombs. Meowscarada sets off the bombs before its foes realize what’s going on.

species.name: Fuecoco
species.desc: The Fire Croc Pokémon. It lies on warm rocks and uses the heat absorbed by its square-shaped scales to create fire energy.

species.name: Crocalor
species.desc: The Fire Croc Pokémon. The combination of Crocalor’s fire energy and overflowing vitality has caused an egg-shaped fireball to appear on the Pokémon’s head.

species.name: Skeledirge
species.desc: The Singer Pokémon. The fiery bird changes shape when Skeledirge sings. Rumor has it that the bird was born when the fireball on Skeledirge’s head gained a soul.

species.name: Quaxly
species.desc: The Duckling Pokémon. This Pokémon migrated to Paldea from distant lands long ago. The gel secreted by its feathers repels water and grime.

species.name: Quaxwell
species.desc: The Practicing Pokémon. These Pokémon constantly run through shallow waters to train their legs, then compete with each other to see which of them kicks most gracefully.

species.name: Quaquaval
species.desc: The Dancer Pokémon. A single kick from a Quaquaval can send a truck rolling. This Pokémon uses its powerful legs to perform striking dances from far-off lands.

species.name: Lechonk
species.desc: The Hog Pokémon. It searches for food all day. It possesses a keen sense of smell but doesn’t use it for anything other than foraging.

species.name: Oinkologne ♀
