species.desc: The Hog Pokémon. This is a meticulous Pokémon that likes to keep things tidy. It shrouds itself in a floral aroma that soothes the Pokémon around it.

species.name: Oinkologne ♂
species.desc: The Hog Pokémon. Oinkologne is proud of its fine, glossy skin. It emits a concentrated scent from the tip of its tail.

species.name: Tarountula
species.desc: The String Ball Pokémon. The ball of threads wrapped around its body is elastic enough to deflect the scythes of Scyther, this Pokémon’s natural enemy.

species.name: Spidops
species.desc: The Trap Pokémon. It clings to branches and ceilings using its threads and moves without a sound. It takes out its prey before the prey even notices it.

species.name: Nymble
species.desc: The Grasshopper Pokémon. It has its third set of legs folded up. When it’s in a tough spot, this Pokémon jumps over 30 feet using the strength of its legs.

species.name: Lokix
species.desc: The Grasshopper Pokémon. When it decides to fight all out, it stands on its previously folded legs to enter Showdown Mode. It neutralizes its enemies in short order.

species.name: Pawmi
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. It has underdeveloped electric sacs on its cheeks. These sacs can produce electricity only if Pawmi rubs them furiously with the pads on its forepaws.

species.name: Pawmo
species.desc: The Mouse Pokémon. When its group is attacked, Pawmo is the first to leap into battle, defeating enemies with a fighting technique that utilizes electric shocks.

species.name: Pawmot
species.desc: The Hands-On Pokémon. This Pokémon normally is slow to react, but once it enters battle, it will strike down its enemies with lightning-fast movements.

species.name: Tandemaus
species.desc: The Couple Pokémon. Exhibiting great teamwork, they use their incisors to cut pieces out of any material that might be useful for a nest, then make off with them.

species.name: Maushold
species.desc: The Family Pokémon. The two little ones just appeared one day. The group might be a family of related Pokémon, but nobody knows for sure.

species.name: Fidough
species.desc: The Puppy Pokémon. This Pokémon is smooth and moist to the touch. Yeast in Fidough’s breath induces fermentation in the Pokémon’s vicinity.

species.name: Dachsbun
species.desc: The Dog Pokémon. The pleasant aroma that emanates from this Pokémon’s body helps wheat grow, so Dachsbun has been treasured by farming villages.

species.name: Smoliv
species.desc: The Olive Pokémon. It protects itself from enemies by emitting oil from the fruit on its head. This oil is bitter and astringent enough to make someone flinch.

species.name: Dolliv
species.desc: The Olive Pokémon. Dolliv shares its tasty, fresh-scented oil with others. This species has coexisted with humans since times long gone.

species.name: Arboliva
species.desc: The Olive Pokémon. This calm Pokémon is very compassionate. It will share its delicious, nutrient-rich oil with weakened Pokémon.

species.name: Squawkabilly
species.desc: The Parrot Pokémon. These Pokémon prefer to live in cities. They form flocks based on the color of their feathers, and they fight over territory.

species.name: Nacli
species.desc: The Rock Salt Pokémon. It was born in a layer of rock salt deep under the earth. This species was particularly treasured in the old days, as they would share precious salt.

species.name: Naclstack
species.desc: The Rock Salt Pokémon. This Pokémon dry cures its prey by spraying salt over them. The curing process steals away the water in the prey’s body.

species.name: Garganacl
species.desc: The Rock Salt Pokémon. Garganacl will rub its fingertips together and sprinkle injured Pokémon with salt. Even severe wounds will promptly heal afterward.

species.name: Charcadet
species.desc: The Fire Child Pokémon. Burnt charcoal came to life and became a Pokémon. Possessing a fiery fighting spirit, Charcadet will battle even tough opponents.

species.name: Armarouge
species.desc: The Fire Warrior Pokémon. Armarouge evolved through the use of a set of armor that belonged to a distinguished warrior. This Pokémon is incredibly loyal.

species.name: Ceruledge
species.desc: The Fire Blades Pokémon. The fiery blades on its arms burn fiercely with the lingering resentment of a sword wielder who fell before accomplishing their goal.

species.name: Tadbulb
species.desc: The EleTadpole Pokémon. Tadbulb shakes its tail to generate electricity. If it senses danger, it will make its head blink on and off to alert its allies.

species.name: Bellibolt
species.desc: The EleFrog Pokémon. When this Pokémon expands and contracts its wobbly body, the belly-button dynamo in its stomach produces a huge amount of electricity.

species.name: Wattrel
species.desc: The Storm Petrel Pokémon. When its wings catch the wind, the bones within produce electricity. This Pokémon dives into the ocean, catching prey by electrocuting them.

species.name: Kilowattrel
species.desc: The Frigatebird Pokémon. Kilowattrel inflates its throat sac to amplify its electricity. By riding the wind, this Pokémon can fly over 430 miles in a day.

species.name: Maschiff
species.desc: The Rascal Pokémon. It always scowls in an attempt to make opponents take it seriously, but even crying children will burst into laughter when they see Maschiff’s face.

species.name: Mabosstiff
species.desc: The Boss Pokémon. This Pokémon can store energy in its large dewlap. Mabosstiff unleashes this energy all at once to blow away enemies.

species.name: Shroodle
species.desc: The Toxic Mouse Pokémon. Though usually a mellow Pokémon, it will sink its sharp, poison-soaked front teeth into any that anger it, causing paralysis in the object of its ire.

species.name: Grafaiai
species.desc: The Toxic Monkey Pokémon. The color of the poisonous saliva depends on what the Pokémon eats. Grafaiai covers its fingers in its saliva and draws patterns on trees in forests.

species.name: Bramblin
species.desc: The Tumbleweed Pokémon. A soul unable to move on to the afterlife was blown around by the wind until it got tangled up with dried grass and became a Pokémon.

species.name: Brambleghast
species.desc: The Tumbleweed Pokémon. It will open the branches of its head to envelop its prey. Once it absorbs all the life energy it needs, it expels the prey and discards it.

species.name: Toedscool
species.desc: The Woodear Pokémon. Toedscool lives in muggy forests. The flaps that fall from its body are chewy and very delicious.

species.name: Toedscruel
species.desc: The Woodear Pokémon. These Pokémon gather into groups and form colonies deep within forests. They absolutely hate it when strangers approach.

species.name: Klawf
species.desc: The Ambush Pokémon. Klawf hangs upside-down from cliffs, waiting for prey. But Klawf can’t remain in this position for long because its blood rushes to its head.

species.name: Capsakid
species.desc: The Spicy Pepper Pokémon. The more sunlight this Pokémon bathes in, the more spicy chemicals are produced by its body, and thus the spicier its moves become.

species.name: Scovillain
species.desc: The Spicy Pepper Pokémon. The red head converts spicy chemicals into fire energy and blasts the surrounding area with a super spicy stream of flame.

species.name: Rellor
species.desc: The Rolling Pokémon. This Pokémon creates a mud ball by mixing sand and dirt with psychic energy. It treasures its mud ball more than its own life.

species.name: Rabsca
species.desc: The Rolling Pokémon. The body that supports the ball barely moves. Therefore, it is thought that the true body of this Pokémon is actually inside the ball.

species.name: Flittle
species.desc: The Frill Pokémon. Flittle’s toes levitate about half an inch above the ground because of the psychic power emitted from the frills on the Pokémon’s belly.

species.name: Espathra
species.desc: The Ostrich Pokémon. It immobilizes opponents by bathing them in psychic power from its large eyes. Despite its appearance, it has a vicious temperament.

species.name: Tinkatink
species.desc: The Metalsmith Pokémon. It swings its handmade hammer around to protect itself, but the hammer is often stolen by Pokémon that eat metal.

species.name: Tinkatuff
species.desc: The Hammer Pokémon. This Pokémon will attack groups of Pawniard and Bisharp, gathering metal from them in order to create a large and sturdy hammer.

species.name: Tinkaton
species.desc: The Hammer Pokémon. This intelligent Pokémon has a very daring disposition. It knocks rocks into the sky with its hammer, aiming for flying Corviknight.

species.name: Wiglett
species.desc: The Garden Eel Pokémon. This Pokémon can pick up the scent of a Veluza just over 65 feet away and will hide itself in the sand.

species.name: Wugtrio
species.desc: The Garden Eel Pokémon. It has a vicious temperament, contrary to what its appearance may suggest. It wraps its long bodies around prey, then drags the prey into its den.

species.name: Bombirdier
species.desc: The Item Drop Pokémon. It gathers things up in an apron made from shed feathers added to the Pokémon’s chest feathers, then drops those things from high places for fun.

species.name: Finizen
species.desc: The Dolphin Pokémon. It likes playing with others of its kind using the water ring on its tail. It uses ultrasonic waves to sense the emotions of other living creatures.

species.name: Palafin
species.desc: The Dolphin Pokémon. This Pokémon changes its appearance if it hears its allies calling for help. Palafin will never show anybody its moment of transformation.

species.name: Varoom
species.desc: The Single-Cyl Pokémon. It is said that this Pokémon was born when an unknown poison Pokémon entered and inspirited an engine left at a scrap-processing factory.

species.name: Revavroom
species.desc: The Multi-Cyl Pokémon. It creates a gas out of poison and minerals from rocks. It then detonates the gas in its cylinders—now numbering eight—to generate energy.

species.name: Cyclizar
species.desc: The Mount Pokémon. Apparently Cyclizar has been allowing people to ride on its back since ancient times. Depictions of this have been found in 10,000-year-old murals.

species.name: Orthworm
species.desc: The Earthworm Pokémon. When attacked, this Pokémon will wield the tendrils on its body like fists and pelt the opponent with a storm of punches.

species.name: Glimmet
species.desc: The Ore Pokémon. It absorbs nutrients from cave walls. The petals it wears are made of crystallized poison.

species.name: Glimmora
species.desc: The Ore Pokémon. When this Pokémon detects danger, it will open up its crystalline petals and fire beams from its conical body.

species.name: Greavard
species.desc: The Ghost Dog Pokémon. It is said that a dog Pokémon that died in the wild without ever interacting with a human was reborn as this Pokémon.

species.name: Houndstone
species.desc: The Ghost Dog Pokémon. Houndstone spends most of its time sleeping in graveyards. Among all the dog Pokémon, this one is most loyal to its master.

species.name: Flamigo
species.desc: The Synchronize Pokémon. This Pokémon apparently ties the base of its neck into a knot so that energy stored in its belly does not escape from its beak.

species.name: Cetoddle
species.desc: The Terra Whale Pokémon. This species left the ocean and began living on land a very long time ago. It seems to be closely related to Wailmer.

species.name: Cetitan
species.desc: The Terra Whale Pokémon. This Pokémon wanders around snowy, icy areas. It protects its body with powerful muscles and a thick layer of fat under its skin.

species.name: Veluza
species.desc: The Jettison Pokémon. When Veluza discards unnecessary flesh, its mind becomes honed and its psychic power increases. The spare flesh has a mild but delicious flavor.

species.name: Dondozo
species.desc: The Big Catfish Pokémon. This Pokémon is a glutton, but it’s bad at getting food. It teams up with a Tatsugiri to catch prey.

species.name: Tatsugiri
species.desc: The Mimicry Pokémon. This is a small dragon Pokémon. It lives inside the mouth of Dondozo to protect itself from enemies on the outside.

species.name: Annihilape
species.desc: The Rage Monkey Pokémon. When its anger rose beyond a critical point, this Pokémon gained power that is unfettered by the limits of its physical body.

species.name: Clodsire
species.desc: The Spiny Fish Pokémon. When attacked, this Pokémon will retaliate by sticking thick spines out from its body. It’s a risky move that puts everything on the line.

species.name: Farigiraf
species.desc: The Long Neck Pokémon. Now that the brain waves from the head and tail are synced up, the psychic power of this Pokémon is 10 times stronger than Girafarig’s.

species.name: Dudunsparce
species.desc: The Land Snake Pokémon. This Pokémon uses its hard tail to make its nest by boring holes into bedrock deep underground. The nest can reach lengths of over six miles.

species.name: Kingambit
species.desc: The Big Blade Pokémon. Only a Bisharp that stands above all others in its vast army can evolve into Kingambit.

species.name: Great Tusk
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. This creature resembles a mysterious Pokémon that, according to a paranormal magazine, has lived since ancient times.

species.name: Scream Tail
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. It resembles a mysterious Pokémon described in a paranormal magazine as a Jigglypuff from one billion years ago.

species.name: Brute Bonnet
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. It bears a slight resemblance to a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a cross between a dinosaur and a mushroom.

species.name: Flutter Mane
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. It has similar features to a ghostly pterosaur that was covered in a paranormal magazine, but the two have little else in common.

species.name: Slither Wing
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. This Pokémon somewhat resembles an ancient form of Volcarona that was introduced in a dubious magazine.

species.name: Sandy Shocks
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. It slightly resembles a Magneton that lived for 10,000 years and was featured in an article in a paranormal magazine.

species.name: Iron Treads
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. This Pokémon closely resembles a scientific weapon that a paranormal magazine claimed was sent to this planet by aliens.

species.name: Iron Bundle
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. Its shape is similar to a robot featured in a paranormal magazine article. The robot was said to have been created by an ancient civilization.

species.name: Iron Hands
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. It is very similar to a cyborg covered exclusively by a paranormal magazine. The cyborg was said to be the modified form of a certain athlete.

species.name: Iron Jugulis
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. It resembles a certain Pokémon introduced in a paranormal magazine, described as the offspring of a Hydreigon that fell in love with a robot.

species.name: Iron Moth
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. This Pokémon resembles an unknown object described in a paranormal magazine as a UFO sent to observe humanity.

species.name: Iron Thorns
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. It has some similarities to a Pokémon introduced in a dubious magazine as a Tyranitar from one billion years into the future.

species.name: Frigibax
species.desc: The Ice Fin Pokémon. Frigibax absorbs heat through its dorsal fin and converts the heat into ice energy. The higher the temperature, the more energy Frigibax stores.

species.name: Arctibax
species.desc: The Ice Fin Pokémon. Arctibax freezes the air around it, protecting its face with an ice mask and turning its dorsal fin into a blade of ice.

species.name: Baxcalibur
species.desc: The Ice Dragon Pokémon. This Pokémon blasts cryogenic air out from its mouth. This air can instantly freeze even liquid-hot lava.

species.name: Gimmighoul (Chest)
species.desc: The Coin Chest Pokémon. This Pokémon was born inside a treasure chest about 1,500 years ago. It sucks the life-force out of scoundrels who try to steal the treasure.
evTo: Gholdengo (level 10, OR earlier than level 10 if given ₽9,999 to consume)

species.name: Gimmighoul (Roaming)
species.desc: The Coin Hunter Pokémon. This Pokémon was born from passion that seeped into a coin. It wanders, apparently seeking to return to the treasure chest it once inhabited.
evTo: Gholdengo (level 10, OR earlier than level 10 if given ₽9,999 to consume)

species.name: Gholdengo
species.desc: The Coin Entity Pokémon. Its body seems to be made up of 1,000 coins. This Pokémon gets along well with others and is quick to make friends with anybody.

species.name: Wo-Chien
species.desc: The Ruinous Pokémon. The grudge of a person punished for writing the king’s evil deeds upon wooden tablets has clad itself in dead leaves to become a Pokémon.

species.name: Chien-Pao
species.desc: The Ruinous Pokémon. This Pokémon can control 100 tons of fallen snow. It plays around innocently by leaping in and out of avalanches it has caused.

species.name: Ting-Lu
species.desc: The Ruinous Pokémon. The fear poured into an ancient ritual vessel has clad itself in rocks and dirt to become a Pokémon.

species.name: Chi-Yu
species.desc: The Ruinous Pokémon. It controls flames burning at over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit. It casually swims through the sea of lava it creates by melting rock and sand.

species.name: Roaring Moon
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. According to an article in a dubious magazine, this Pokémon has some connection to a phenomenon that occurs in a certain region.

species.name: Iron Valiant
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. It has some similarities to a mad scientist’s invention covered in a paranormal magazine.

species.name: Koraidon
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. This seems to be the Winged King mentioned in an old expedition journal. It was said to have split the land with its bare fists.

species.name: Miraidon
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.

species.name: Walking Wake
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. This ferocious creature is shrouded in mystery. It's named after an aquatic monster mentioned in an old expedition journal.

species.name: Iron Leaves
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.

species.name: Dipplin
species.desc: The Candy Apple Pokémon. Dipplin is two creatures in one Pokémon. Its evolution was triggered by a special apple grown only in one place.

species.name: Poltchageist
species.desc: The Matcha Pokémon. Supposedly, the regrets of a tea ceremony master who died before perfecting his craft lingered in some matcha and became a Pokémon.

species.name: Sinistcha
species.desc: The Matcha Pokémon. It pretends to be tea, trying to fool people into drinking it so it can drain their life-force. Its ruse is generally unsuccessful.

species.name: Okidogi
species.desc: The Retainer Pokémon. After all its muscles were stimulated by the toxic chain around its neck, Okidogi transformed and gained a powerful physique.

species.name: Munkidori
species.desc: The Retainer Pokémon. The chain is made from toxins that enhance capabilities. It stimulated Munkidori's brain and caused the Pokémon's psychic powers to bloom.

species.name: Fezandipiti
species.desc: The Retainer Pokémon. Fezandipiti owes its beautiful looks and lovely voice to the toxic stimulants emanating from the chain wrapped around its body.

species.name: Ogerpon (Cornerstone Mask)
species.desc: The Mask Pokémon. This Pokémon's type changes based on which mask it's wearing. It confounds its enemies with nimble movements and kicks.

species.name: Ogerpon (Heartflame Mask)
species.desc: The Mask Pokémon. This Pokémon's type changes based on which mask it's wearing. It confounds its enemies with nimble movements and kicks.

species.name: Ogerpon (Teal Mask)
species.desc: The Mask Pokémon. This Pokémon's type changes based on which mask it's wearing. It confounds its enemies with nimble movements and kicks.

species.name: Ogerpon (Wellspring Mask)
species.desc: The Mask Pokémon. This Pokémon's type changes based on which mask it's wearing. It confounds its enemies with nimble movements and kicks.

species.name: Archaludon
species.desc: The Alloy Pokémon. It gathers static electricity from its surroundings. The beams it launches when down on all fours are tremendously powerful.

species.name: Hydrapple
species.desc: The Apple Hydra Pokémon. Seven syrpents live inside an apple made of syrup. The syrpent in the center is the commander.

species.name: Gouging Fire
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. There are scant few reports of this creature being sighted. One short video shows it rampaging and spouting pillars of flame.

species.name: Raging Bolt
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. It's said to incinerate everything around it with lightning launched from its fur. Very little is known about this creature.

species.name: Iron Boulder
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. It was named after a mysterious object recorded in an old book. Its body seems to be metallic.

species.name: Iron Crown
species.desc: The Paradox Pokémon. There was supposedly an incident in which it launched shining blades to cut everything around it to pieces. Little else is known about it.

species.name: Terapagos
species.desc: The Tera Pokémon. Terapagos protects itself using its power to transform energy into hard crystals. This Pokémon is the source of the Terastal phenomenon.

species.name: Terapagos (Stellar)
species.desc: The Tera Pokémon. Terapagos protects itself using its power to transform energy into hard crystals. This Pokémon is the source of the Terastal phenomenon.

species.name: Terapagos (Terastal)
species.desc: The Tera Pokémon. Terapagos protects itself using its power to transform energy into hard crystals. This Pokémon is the source of the Terastal phenomenon.

species.name: Pecharunt
species.desc: The Subjugation Pokémon. It feeds others toxic mochi that draw out desires and capabilities. Those who eat the mochi fall under Pecharunt’s control, chained to its will.
